events.title: The War of the Golden Stool
events.body: When the British governor demands to sit on the Golden Stool, the sacred throne of the Asante, Yaa Asantewaa, queen mother of Ejisu, leads an uprising. She is captured and exiled to the Seychelles.

events.title: The British Take Pretoria
events.body: In the South African War, British forces occupy the Transvaal capital. The Boer commandos turn to guerrilla war, and Britain answers with farm burning and concentration camps, where tens of thousands of Boer and Black African civilians die.

events.title: The Boxer Rebellion
events.body: An anti-foreign uprising in northern China besieges the foreign legations in Beijing. Eight foreign powers send troops to crush it and impose heavy reparations.

events.title: The Quantum Is Born
events.body: Max Planck proposes that energy is given off in tiny packets, or quanta, to explain the light from hot objects. It is the seed of quantum physics.

events.title: Australia Federates
events.body: Six British colonies join to form the Commonwealth of Australia. One of its first laws restricts immigration to keep the country white.

events.title: Queen Victoria Dies
events.body: Britain's longest-reigning monarch until then dies after 63 years on the throne, at the height of the British Empire.

events.title: The First Nobel Prizes
events.body: The first Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm and Oslo, funded by the will of Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite.

events.title: Radio Crosses the Atlantic
events.body: Guglielmo Marconi reports receiving the Morse letter 'S' in Newfoundland, sent by radio from Cornwall across the Atlantic.

events.title: Mount Pelée
events.body: A glowing cloud of gas and ash from Mount Pelée sweeps over Saint-Pierre, Martinique, killing about 28,000 people — almost the whole town.

events.title: The Treaty of Vereeniging
events.body: The South African War ends with the Boer republics surrendering to Britain. The peace leaves the question of Black South Africans' rights to a future white government.

events.title: Os Sertões
events.body: Euclides da Cunha, who reported on the war, publishes Rebellion in the Backlands, his account of Canudos — a founding book of modern Brazil.

events.title: The First Tour de France
events.body: Sixty riders set off from outside Paris on a race around France, organised to sell more copies of a sports newspaper.

events.title: The Suffragettes Organise
events.body: Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women's Social and Political Union in Manchester, with the motto "Deeds, not words".

events.title: Panama Separates from Colombia
events.body: With US warships close by, Panama declares independence. Within weeks it signs a treaty giving the United States the Canal Zone.

events.title: The First Powered Flight
events.body: At Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flies a powered aeroplane for 12 seconds. By the end of the day, his brother Wilbur manages 59.

events.title: The Herero and Nama Genocide
events.body: The Herero rise against German rule in South West Africa (now Namibia). Germany's response, including an order to exterminate them, kills tens of thousands of Herero and Nama people — the first genocide of the 20th century.

events.title: The Cherry Orchard
events.body: Chekhov's last play, about an aristocratic family losing its estate, premieres at the Moscow Art Theatre under Stanislavski.

events.title: The Casement Report
events.body: British consul Roger Casement's report on the Congo Free State documents the floggings, mutilations and killings behind the rubber trade, and fuels an international campaign.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in St Petersburg
events.body: Troops fire on workers marching peacefully to petition the Tsar. The massacre sets off the 1905 Revolution, which forces Russia's first parliament.

events.title: Japan Defeats Russia at Tsushima
events.body: Japan's navy destroys Russia's Baltic fleet. It is the first modern victory of an Asian power over a European one, watched closely across the colonised world.

events.title: Einstein's Miracle Year
events.body: A 26-year-old clerk at the Swiss patent office publishes four papers, on light, atoms, special relativity and E = mc². Physics is never the same.

events.title: The Maji Maji Rebellion
events.body: Peoples of southern German East Africa rise against forced cotton growing, trusting in sacred water to turn bullets to water. German scorched-earth tactics bring famine; estimates of the dead range from 75,000 to 300,000.

events.title: The Partition of Bengal
events.body: Viceroy Curzon splits Bengal in two. The Swadeshi movement answers with a boycott of British goods, and the partition is reversed in 1911.

events.title: The San Francisco Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake and the fires that follow destroy most of San Francisco. Around 3,000 people die.

events.title: Persia's Constitutional Revolution
events.body: After mass protests, the Shah agrees to an elected parliament, the Majlis — one of the first in Asia.

events.title: Gandhi Launches Satyagraha
events.body: At a mass meeting in Johannesburg against a law forcing Indians to register, Mohandas Gandhi and the crowd pledge to resist without violence — the start of satyagraha.

events.title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
events.body: Pablo Picasso paints five women in broken, angular planes, with faces drawing on African and Iberian masks. It points the way to Cubism.

events.title: Budi Utomo
events.body: Students in Batavia found the first modern Indonesian nationalist organisation. 20 May is still National Awakening Day.

events.title: Oil in Persia
events.body: British prospectors strike oil at Masjed Soleyman. The Anglo-Persian Oil Company, later BP, follows.

events.title: The Tunguska Event
events.body: A huge explosion — probably an asteroid or comet bursting in the air — flattens some 80 million trees over remote Siberia.

events.title: The Young Turk Revolution
events.body: Army officers of the Committee of Union and Progress force Abdul Hamid II to restore the constitution.

events.title: The Model T
events.body: Henry Ford launches the Model T. With the moving assembly line from 1913, the car becomes something ordinary families can buy.

events.title: Belgium Takes Over the Congo
events.body: Under international pressure, Leopold II hands the Congo to the Belgian state. It becomes the Belgian Congo.

events.title: The Messina Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina in Sicily and Reggio Calabria, killing about 75,000 people or more.

events.title: The Union of South Africa
events.body: Four British colonies unite as the Union of South Africa, with Louis Botha as prime minister. Black South Africans are shut out of power in most of the country.

events.title: The Putumayo Atrocities
events.body: Roger Casement investigates a British-registered rubber company in the Peruvian Amazon, which enslaves Indigenous people and kills thousands. His report, published in 1912, shocks Britain.

events.title: Japan Annexes Korea
events.body: Japan formally annexes Korea, beginning 35 years of colonial rule.

events.title: The Mexican Revolution Begins
events.body: Francisco Madero calls for an uprising against the long dictatorship of Porfirio Díaz. A decade of revolution follows, with Emiliano Zapata fighting for land for peasants.

events.title: The Atomic Nucleus
events.body: In Manchester, Ernest Rutherford explains why a few alpha particles bounce back from gold foil: almost all of an atom's mass sits in a tiny, dense nucleus.

events.title: Machu Picchu Reaches the World
events.body: Guided by local farmers who knew it well, American explorer Hiram Bingham reaches the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu and makes it famous abroad.

events.title: China's Revolution
events.body: An uprising in Wuchang brings down the Qing dynasty, which had ruled China since 1644. The boy emperor Puyi abdicates in February 1912.

events.title: The First Air Raid
events.body: During Italy's invasion of Ottoman Libya, Lieutenant Giulio Gavotti drops grenades from his plane on an Ottoman camp — the first bombing from an aircraft.

events.title: Amundsen Reaches the South Pole
events.body: Roald Amundsen's Norwegian team reaches the South Pole by dog sled. Robert Falcon Scott's British party arrives five weeks later; all five die on the way back.

events.title: Continental Drift
events.body: In a lecture in Frankfurt, Alfred Wegener proposes that the continents were once joined and have drifted apart. Most geologists reject the idea until the 1960s.

events.title: The ANC Is Founded
events.body: Chiefs, lawyers, teachers and church leaders meet in Bloemfontein to form the South African Native National Congress, later the ANC, to fight for Black South Africans' rights.

events.title: The Titanic Sinks
events.body: The 'unsinkable' liner strikes an iceberg on her maiden voyage and sinks in under three hours. More than 1,500 people die; there are lifeboats for barely half on board.

events.title: The Rite of Spring
events.body: The premiere of Stravinsky's ballet, with its pounding rhythms and Nijinsky's jagged choreography, causes uproar in a Paris theatre.

events.title: Emily Davison at the Derby
events.body: Suffragette Emily Wilding Davison steps in front of the King's horse at the Epsom Derby and dies of her injuries four days later.

events.title: The Natives Land Act
events.body: South Africa's parliament bans Black South Africans from buying or renting land outside reserves covering about 7% of the country. Sol Plaatje writes that the Black South African woke up 'not actually a slave, but a pariah in the land of his birth'.

events.title: Fertiliser From the Air
events.body: The first factory using the Haber–Bosch process opens in Germany, making ammonia from nitrogen in the air. Synthetic fertiliser later feeds billions — and the same chemistry supplies explosives for war.

events.title: A Nobel for Tagore
events.body: Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore becomes the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, for Gitanjali.

events.title: Swann's Way
events.body: Marcel Proust publishes, at his own expense, the first volume of In Search of Lost Time, set off by the taste of a madeleine dipped in tea.

events.title: Gandhi Leads the Great March
events.body: Gandhi leads thousands of Indian mine workers and their families on a march from Natal into the Transvaal, defying the law. Their strike forces the government to compromise.

events.title: The Moving Assembly Line
events.body: Ford's Highland Park plant starts a moving assembly line, cutting the time to build a Model T from about twelve hours to about an hour and a half.

events.title: The First Crossword
events.body: The New York World prints Arthur Wynne's 'word-cross' puzzle. Within a decade, crosswords are a craze.

events.title: The First Airline Flight
events.body: The St Petersburg–Tampa Airboat Line carries its first paying passenger across Tampa Bay — 23 minutes, one passenger, and the birth of scheduled air travel.

events.title: Nigeria Amalgamated
events.body: Frederick Lugard joins Britain's northern and southern protectorates into one colony, Nigeria.

events.title: The Tramp First Appears
events.body: Charlie Chaplin's Little Tramp shuffles onto screen in Kid Auto Races at Venice — bowler, cane and all. Within two years he is the most famous face on Earth.

events.title: The Rokeby Venus Slashed
events.body: Suffragette Mary Richardson attacks Velázquez's masterpiece in the National Gallery with a meat cleaver, protesting Emmeline Pankhurst's imprisonment.

events.title: The King at the Cup Final
events.body: George V becomes the first reigning monarch to attend an FA Cup final, watching Burnley beat Liverpool 1–0 at Crystal Palace.

events.title: Franz Ferdinand Assassinated
events.body: Gavrilo Princip shoots the Austro-Hungarian heir and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo. The driver had taken a wrong turn. Within six weeks, Europe is at war.

events.title: The National Party Founded
events.body: General JBM Hertzog founds the National Party in Bloemfontein — the party that will rule South Africa from 1948 and build apartheid.

events.title: Gandhi Leaves South Africa
events.body: After 21 years, Mohandas Gandhi sails from Cape Town for the last time. The methods of satyagraha, forged against South African race laws, go with him to India.

events.title: Austria-Hungary Declares War
events.body: One month after Sarajevo, Vienna declares war on Serbia and shells Belgrade. The alliances begin to pull every great power in.

events.title: The London Stock Exchange Closes
events.body: Panic selling forces the Exchange to shut for the first time in its history. It stays closed for five months; New York follows the same day.

events.title: Germany Declares War on Russia
events.body: The Tsar's mobilisation triggers Germany's declaration. France mobilises the same day. The continental war is now unstoppable.

events.title: Britain Declares War on Germany
events.body: Germany invades neutral Belgium; Britain's ultimatum expires at 23:00. "The lamps are going out all over Europe," says Foreign Secretary Edward Grey.

events.title: The First Electric Traffic Light
events.body: Cleveland, Ohio installs the world's first electric traffic signal at Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street — red and green, with a warning buzzer.

events.title: Endurance Sets Sail
events.body: Ernest Shackleton's Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition leaves Plymouth — toward one of the greatest survival stories ever lived.

events.title: The Panama Canal Opens
events.body: The SS Ancon makes the first official transit, joining the Atlantic and Pacific. Ten years of American engineering — and thousands of workers' lives — behind it.

events.title: The Battle of Mons
events.body: The British Expeditionary Force fights its first battle of the war, its riflemen firing so fast the Germans believe they face machine guns.

events.title: The Library of Louvain Burns
events.body: German troops torch the Belgian university library — 300,000 books and irreplaceable mediaeval manuscripts lost in a night that shocks the world.

events.title: The Last Passenger Pigeon Dies
events.body: Martha, the last of a species that once darkened American skies in the billions, dies in Cincinnati Zoo — extinction's most famous single moment.

events.title: Benedict XV Elected Pope
events.body: Giacomo della Chiesa becomes pope as Europe burns. He calls the war "the suicide of civilised Europe" and spends his papacy pleading for peace.

events.title: The Battle of the Marne
events.body: French and British forces stop the German sweep towards Paris; Parisian taxis ferry troops to the front. The war of movement ends — the trenches begin.

events.title: Home Rule — Passed and Frozen
events.body: Irish Home Rule finally receives royal assent after decades of struggle, then is immediately suspended for the war — a postponement with fateful consequences.

events.title: The Maritz Rebellion
events.body: Martial law is declared in South Africa as Boer officers rise against joining Britain's war on Germany. The revolt is crushed by year's end.

events.title: First Ypres Begins
events.body: The armies dig in around the Flemish town where so much of the war's horror will concentrate. By its end, the old British regular army has effectively ceased to exist.

events.title: The East African Campaign
events.body: The First World War reaches East Africa with a British landing at Tanga. German forces fight on until after the armistice; tens of thousands of African carriers die of disease, hunger and exhaustion — by some estimates over 100,000.

events.title: The Christmas Truce
events.body: Along stretches of the Western Front, the guns fall silent. Soldiers sing carols, swap tobacco, bury their dead — and, in places, play football between the trenches.

events.title: The Armenian Genocide
events.body: Ottoman authorities arrest Armenian leaders in Constantinople, the start of deportations and massacres in which hundreds of thousands — by many estimates over a million — Armenians die.

events.title: The Gallipoli Landings
events.body: British, French, Australian, New Zealand and Indian troops land at Gallipoli to knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. The campaign fails after eight months; Anzac Day remembers it.

events.title: The Lusitania Sunk
events.body: A German submarine sinks the British liner Lusitania off Ireland. Of the nearly 1,200 people killed, 128 are Americans, turning US opinion against Germany.

events.title: General Relativity
events.body: Einstein completes his theory of gravity: mass bends space and time, and light bends around the Sun. A 1919 eclipse confirms it.

events.title: The Metamorphosis
events.body: Franz Kafka publishes the story of a travelling salesman who wakes up as a monstrous insect, and of his family's reaction.

events.title: The US Occupies Haiti
events.body: US Marines land in Haiti after its president is killed by a mob. The occupation lasts nineteen years.

events.title: Dada Opens in Zürich
events.body: Artists who fled the war open the Cabaret Voltaire in Zürich, staging nonsense poetry and anti-art — Dada, a howl against the logic that led to the slaughter.

events.title: The Battle of Verdun
events.body: Germany attacks the French fortress city of Verdun. The battle lasts ten months and kills or wounds about 700,000 men.

events.title: The Easter Rising
events.body: Irish republicans seize central Dublin and proclaim an Irish Republic. The rising is crushed in six days, but the execution of its leaders turns Irish opinion towards independence.

events.title: The Sykes–Picot Agreement
events.body: Britain and France secretly agree how to divide the Ottoman Empire's Arab lands between them. Its lines shape the borders of the modern Middle East.

events.title: The Arab Revolt
events.body: Sharif Hussein of Mecca leads an Arab uprising against Ottoman rule, backed by Britain, which has promised Arab independence — while secretly agreeing Sykes–Picot.

events.title: The First Day of the Somme
events.body: The British army suffers nearly 60,000 casualties in a single day, the worst in its history. The Somme offensive grinds on until November.

sources.title: What happened during the Battle of the Somme

events.title: The Central Asian Revolt
events.body: An order drafting Muslim men for labour behind the First World War front sparks risings among Kazakhs and Kyrgyz. Russian reprisals follow; huge numbers flee across the mountains to China, and many die. The Kyrgyz remember it as Ürkün.

events.title: The Tsar Abdicates
events.body: Bread riots and mutinies in Petrograd force Nicholas II to abdicate, ending three centuries of Romanov rule.

events.title: America Enters the War
events.body: The United States declares war on Germany after unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram.

events.title: Duchamp's Fountain
events.body: Marcel Duchamp submits a porcelain urinal signed 'R. Mutt' to an art exhibition in New York. It is rejected — and becomes one of the most influential works of modern art.

events.title: The Visions at Fátima
events.body: Three shepherd children in Portugal report seeing the Virgin Mary. Fátima becomes one of the great Catholic pilgrimage sites.

events.title: Wilfred Owen's War Poems
events.body: Recovering from shell shock at Craiglockhart hospital in Edinburgh, Wilfred Owen drafts 'Dulce et Decorum Est' and 'Anthem for Doomed Youth'. He is killed a week before the Armistice; his poems are published after his death.

events.title: The Balfour Declaration
events.body: Britain declares support for 'a national home for the Jewish people' in Palestine, while promising not to prejudice the rights of its existing non-Jewish communities.

events.title: The Bolshevik Revolution
events.body: Lenin's Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd. Within months Russia leaves the war, and civil war begins.

events.title: The Halifax Explosion
events.body: A French munitions ship collides with another vessel in Halifax harbour, Canada, and explodes — the largest human-made explosion before the atomic bomb. About 2,000 people die.

events.title: The Spanish Flu
events.body: A deadly flu spreads around the world in three waves, carried by troops and ships. It infects about a third of humanity and kills tens of millions — more than the war.

events.title: The Romanovs Shot
events.body: Bolshevik guards shoot the former Tsar Nicholas II, his wife and their five children in a cellar in Yekaterinburg.

events.title: Influenza in Samoa
events.body: The ship Talune brings the flu to Western Samoa, then under New Zealand rule. About a fifth of the population dies; American Samoa, which closes its ports, has no deaths.

events.title: The Armistice
events.body: At 11 o'clock, the guns fall silent on the Western Front. Around 20 million soldiers and civilians have died in the war.

sources.title: Conditions of the Armistice with Germany (11 November 1918)
sources.publisher: German History in Documents and Images

sources.title: Milestones to Peace: the Armistice of Compiègne

events.title: British Women Vote
events.body: For the first time, British women over 30 who meet a property qualification vote in a general election. Some other countries, like New Zealand, got there decades earlier.

events.title: Rosa Luxemburg Murdered
events.body: The socialist leader is killed by right-wing paramilitaries in Berlin after a failed uprising, as Germany's new republic begins in violence.

events.title: The March First Movement
events.body: Koreans declare independence from Japanese rule in peaceful protests across the country. Japan crushes them, killing thousands.

events.title: Egypt's 1919 Revolution
events.body: When Britain exiles the nationalist leader Saad Zaghloul, Egyptians of every class — Muslims and Copts, men and women — strike and protest. Britain grants Egypt limited independence in 1922.

events.title: The Amritsar Massacre
events.body: British troops fire without warning on an unarmed crowd in the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing hundreds. Tagore returns his knighthood; Indian opinion turns against British rule.

events.title: The Bauhaus
events.body: Walter Gropius founds an art school in Weimar that joins craft, art and industry. Its plain, functional design shapes modern buildings and furniture worldwide.

events.title: The May Fourth Movement
events.body: Students in Beijing protest the Versailles decision to hand German concessions in China to Japan. The movement shapes modern Chinese nationalism and communism.

events.title: The Eclipse That Proved Einstein
events.body: Expeditions to the island of Príncipe and to Sobral in Brazil photograph a solar eclipse and find starlight bent by the Sun, as general relativity predicts.

events.title: A Petition at Versailles
events.body: A young Vietnamese living in Paris, later known as Ho Chi Minh, sends the peace conference a petition asking for Vietnamese rights. It is ignored.

events.title: The Treaty of Versailles
events.body: Germany signs a peace that takes its colonies and some territory, limits its army and makes it accept blame and pay reparations. Its harshness is later blamed for the rise of Hitler.

sources.title: The Versailles Treaty, 28 June 1919 — Part III

events.title: The League of Nations
events.body: The world's first permanent organisation for keeping the peace is founded in Geneva. The United States, whose president proposed it, never joins.

sources.title: The Covenant of the League of Nations

events.title: Prohibition
events.body: The sale of alcohol is banned across the United States. It feeds organised crime and speakeasies until repeal in 1933.

events.title: American Women Win the Vote
events.body: The 19th Amendment is ratified, giving women in the United States the vote — though Black women in the South remain largely shut out for decades.

events.title: Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement
events.body: The Indian National Congress backs Gandhi's call to boycott British courts, schools, goods and titles. Millions take part.

events.title: The Bulhoek Massacre
events.body: South African police open fire on a religious community, the Israelites, who refused to leave land at Bulhoek near Queenstown. More than 160 are killed.

events.title: The Chinese Communist Party Founded
events.body: A dozen delegates, among them Mao Zedong, meet secretly in Shanghai to found the Chinese Communist Party.

events.title: Insulin Discovered
events.body: In Toronto, Frederick Banting and Charles Best extract insulin. Within a year it is saving the lives of children with diabetes who would otherwise have died.

events.title: The Disaster of Annual
events.body: Rif fighters led by Abd el-Krim rout a Spanish army in northern Morocco; thousands of Spanish soldiers die. Abd el-Krim declares a Rif Republic.

events.title: Simon Kimbangu
events.body: A Baptist catechist whose healings draw thousands is sentenced by the Belgian authorities; he dies in prison thirty years later. The church named after him grows into one of Africa's largest.

events.title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty
events.body: Irish and British negotiators, including Michael Collins, sign the treaty creating the Irish Free State. Disagreement over it leads to the Irish Civil War.

events.title: Ulysses
events.body: James Joyce's novel following one Dublin day, 16 June 1904, is published in Paris. Banned for years in Britain and the US, it changes the novel.

events.title: Modern Art Week
events.body: A week of exhibitions, concerts and readings in São Paulo launches Brazilian modernism.

events.title: The Rand Revolt
events.body: White mine workers on the Witwatersrand strike against plans to replace them with cheaper Black workers. Prime Minister Smuts sends in the army and aircraft; more than 200 die.

events.title: The Harry Thuku Protest
events.body: After the arrest of Harry Thuku, who campaigned against forced labour and pass laws, a crowd gathers outside Nairobi's police station. Police open fire, killing at least 21 people.

events.title: The Waste Land
events.body: T. S. Eliot's poem of fragments — voices, myths and ruins — becomes the defining poem of a broken post-war world.

events.title: Nosferatu
events.body: F. W. Murnau's silent vampire film, an unauthorised take on Dracula, becomes a landmark of German Expressionist cinema.

events.title: The March on Rome
events.body: Benito Mussolini's Fascist blackshirts march on Rome; the King hands him power. The first fascist government in Europe begins.

events.title: Tutankhamun's Tomb Found
events.body: Howard Carter's team finds the steps to the nearly intact tomb of the boy pharaoh Tutankhamun in Egypt's Valley of the Kings.

events.title: The Soviet Union Is Formed
events.body: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian republics join to form the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.

events.title: The Great Kantō Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake and firestorms destroy much of Tokyo and Yokohama, killing over 100,000 people. In the chaos, mobs murder thousands of Korean residents.

events.title: The Turkish Republic
events.body: Mustafa Kemal proclaims the Republic of Turkey from the ruins of the Ottoman Empire, with Ankara as its capital.

events.title: The Beer Hall Putsch
events.body: Adolf Hitler's Nazis try to seize power in Munich and fail. In prison he writes Mein Kampf.

events.title: Germany's Hyperinflation
events.body: The German mark collapses: a loaf of bread costs billions of marks, and people paid in the morning rush to spend before prices rise again.

events.title: Lenin Dies
events.body: The founder of the Soviet state dies after a series of strokes. Stalin outmanoeuvres his rivals and by the end of the decade rules alone.

events.title: The First Winter Olympics
events.body: The first Winter Olympic Games open in Chamonix in the French Alps.

events.title: Rhapsody in Blue
events.body: George Gershwin's piece blending jazz and the concert hall premieres in New York, opening with its famous clarinet wail.

events.title: The Blues Craze
events.body: Bessie Smith, 'the Empress of the Blues', becomes the best-paid Black entertainer of the age, as records carry blues and jazz from the American South around the world.

events.title: The Harlem Renaissance
events.body: The Survey Graphic's special issue 'Harlem: Mecca of the New Negro', soon expanded as The New Negro, announces a flowering of Black American writing, art and music.

events.title: The Great Gatsby
events.body: F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel of wealth, longing and illusion in the Jazz Age is published to modest sales; it later becomes an American classic.

events.title: Louis Armstrong's Hot Five
events.body: Louis Armstrong's Hot Five recordings make the improvised solo the heart of jazz.

events.title: The Scopes Trial
events.body: A Tennessee teacher is convicted of teaching evolution in a public school, in a trial broadcast on radio and watched by the world.

events.title: Josephine Baker in Paris
events.body: Josephine Baker opens in La Revue Nègre and becomes the star of Paris. She later works for the French Resistance and the American civil rights movement.

events.title: Battleship Potemkin
events.body: Sergei Eisenstein's film of the 1905 mutiny, with its massacre on the Odessa Steps, shows what montage can do and becomes one of the most studied films ever.

events.title: Television Demonstrated
events.body: John Logie Baird demonstrates moving pictures sent by television to scientists in his attic workshop in London's Soho.

events.title: The British General Strike
events.body: About 1.7 million workers strike in support of miners facing wage cuts. The strike collapses after nine days.

events.title: The Cristero War
events.body: As Mexico's government enforces harsh laws against the Church, priests stop holding services and Catholic rebels take up arms. Tens of thousands die before a settlement in 1929.

events.title: The Little Black Dress
events.body: American Vogue publishes Coco Chanel's simple black dress and calls it 'Chanel's Ford' — a design anyone could wear, and a staple ever since.

events.title: Metropolis
events.body: Fritz Lang's vast science-fiction film of a city split between rich thinkers above and workers below premieres in Berlin.

events.title: The Hujum
events.body: On International Women's Day, the Soviet authorities in Uzbekistan launch a campaign for women to cast off the full veil. Many women who unveil are murdered in the backlash.

events.title: The Shanghai Massacre
events.body: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists turn on their Communist allies in Shanghai, killing thousands. China's civil war begins.

events.title: Lindbergh Flies the Atlantic
events.body: Charles Lindbergh lands in Paris after flying alone and non-stop from New York in 33½ hours.

events.title: The Uncertainty Principle
events.body: Werner Heisenberg shows that a particle's position and speed cannot both be known exactly. At a famous conference in Brussels that year, physicists argue over what quantum mechanics means.

events.title: To the Lighthouse
events.body: Virginia Woolf's novel, told through the shifting thoughts of a family on holiday, with the war passing in a few short pages, is published.

events.title: Sandino's Rebellion
events.body: Augusto Sandino's guerrillas attack US Marines occupying Nicaragua at Ocotal. The Marines leave in 1933; Sandino is murdered in 1934, and later revolutionaries take his name.

events.title: The Jazz Singer
events.body: The first feature film with synchronised talking and singing sequences opens in New York. Silent cinema's days are numbered.

events.title: The Muslim Brotherhood Founded
events.body: Schoolteacher Hassan al-Banna founds the Muslim Brotherhood in Ismailia, Egypt. It becomes one of the most influential Islamist movements in the world.

events.title: The Threepenny Opera
events.body: Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill's play with songs, set among beggars and thieves, opens in Berlin. 'Mack the Knife' becomes a standard.

events.title: India Wins Olympic Hockey Gold
events.body: India wins the field hockey gold at the Amsterdam Olympics without conceding a goal, the first of six golds in a row.

events.title: The Coniston Massacre
events.body: After a dingo trapper is killed, a police-led party kills Warlpiri, Anmatyerre and Kaytetye people in the Northern Territory — officially 31, probably many more. It is the last known officially sanctioned massacre of Aboriginal people.

events.title: Penicillin Discovered
events.body: Alexander Fleming notices mould killing bacteria on a dish left out in his London laboratory. Penicillin becomes the first antibiotic.

events.title: The Youth Pledge
events.body: A youth congress in Batavia pledges one motherland, one nation and one language: Indonesia. The anthem 'Indonesia Raya' is played for the first time.

events.title: Steamboat Willie
events.body: Mickey Mouse whistles his way into cinemas in one of the first cartoons with synchronised sound.

events.title: All Quiet on the Western Front
events.body: Erich Maria Remarque's novel of an ordinary German soldier's war is a worldwide bestseller. The Nazis later burn it.

events.title: The Expanding Universe
events.body: Edwin Hubble shows that distant galaxies are moving away from us, and the further away they are, the faster — the universe is expanding.

events.title: The Wall Street Crash
events.body: Panic selling on the New York Stock Exchange starts the crash that leads into the Great Depression, which spreads around the world.

events.title: The Aba Women's War
events.body: Thousands of Igbo and Ibibio women in south-eastern Nigeria protest against British colonial taxes and appointed chiefs. Troops kill dozens of them.

events.title: Black Saturday in Samoa
events.body: New Zealand police fire on a peaceful procession of the Mau independence movement in Apia, killing its leader Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III and others.

events.title: India Declares for Full Independence
events.body: At Lahore, the Indian National Congress, led by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopts the goal of Purna Swaraj — complete independence — and raises the flag of India.

events.title: Pluto Discovered
events.body: Clyde Tombaugh, a 24-year-old farm boy, spots a new planet on photographic plates at Lowell Observatory in Arizona. It is later reclassified as a dwarf planet.

events.title: The Salt March
events.body: Gandhi sets off on a 24-day walk to the sea at Dandi to make salt in defiance of the British salt tax. Tens of thousands are arrested in the protests that follow.

events.title: The Kazakh Famine
events.body: Forced settlement of nomads and seizure of their herds bring famine to Kazakhstan. About a million and a half people die — roughly a third or more of all Kazakhs.

events.title: The First World Cup Final
events.body: Hosts Uruguay beat Argentina 4–2 in Montevideo to win the first FIFA World Cup.

events.title: The Empire State Building
events.body: The world's tallest building opens in New York, built in just over a year during the Depression.

events.title: Diego Rivera's Murals
events.body: Mexican muralist Diego Rivera, whose public walls tell Mexico's history from the side of workers and Indigenous people, is honoured with a solo show at New York's Museum of Modern Art.

events.title: Omar Mukhtar Hanged
events.body: After twenty years leading Libyan resistance against Italian rule, 73-year-old Omar Mukhtar is captured and hanged in front of thousands of people held in Italian camps.

events.title: Japan Invades Manchuria
events.body: Japanese officers blow up a railway line near Mukden and blame China, using it as a pretext to seize Manchuria. The League of Nations does little.

events.title: The Sydney Harbour Bridge
events.body: The steel arch bridge opens. Before the premier can cut the ribbon, a man on horseback slashes it with his sword.

events.title: The Siamese Revolution
events.body: A small group of officers and officials stage a bloodless coup that ends absolute monarchy in Siam, now Thailand.

events.title: The Holodomor
events.body: Stalin's forced collectivisation and grain seizures cause famine in Soviet Ukraine and Kazakhstan. Millions die in 1932–33; Ukraine remembers it as the Holodomor.

events.title: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
events.body: Ibn Saud unites his conquests as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Six years later, American geologists strike oil.

events.title: Hitler Becomes Chancellor
events.body: Germany's president appoints Adolf Hitler chancellor. Within months the Nazis ban other parties, open the first concentration camp at Dachau and boycott Jewish businesses.

events.title: The New Deal
events.body: Franklin D. Roosevelt takes office telling Americans 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself', and launches public works and relief to fight the Depression.

events.title: The Nazi Book Burnings
events.body: Students and Nazi officials burn tens of thousands of 'un-German' books across Germany, including works by Jewish, socialist and pacifist writers.

events.title: The Dust Bowl
events.body: Drought and over-ploughed prairie turn the US Great Plains into a dust bowl. Huge 'black blizzards' blow soil as far as the Atlantic, and families flee west.

events.title: The Long March
events.body: Encircled by Nationalist forces, China's Communists begin a year-long retreat of thousands of kilometres. Mao Zedong emerges as their leader.

events.title: Négritude
events.body: Aimé Césaire, Léopold Sédar Senghor and other Black students in Paris launch the journal L'Étudiant noir and the Négritude movement, reclaiming African identity against colonial racism.

events.title: Monopoly
events.body: Parker Brothers begin selling Monopoly, adapted from Lizzie Magie's Landlord's Game, which she designed to show the harm of land monopolies.

events.title: The Nuremberg Laws
events.body: Nazi Germany strips Jews of citizenship and bans marriage between Jews and other Germans.

events.title: Italy Invades Ethiopia
events.body: Mussolini's army invades Ethiopia, one of the last African states free of colonial rule, using poison gas. Haile Selassie appeals in vain to the League of Nations.

events.title: The Arab Revolt in Palestine
events.body: Palestinian Arabs begin a general strike and revolt against British rule and Jewish immigration. Britain crushes it by 1939.

events.title: South Africa Removes the Cape Vote
events.body: Hertzog's government takes Black voters in the Cape off the common voters' roll, removing the last direct vote Black South Africans had in parliament.

events.title: Turing's Computing Machine
events.body: Alan Turing describes an imaginary machine that can carry out any calculation — the idea behind every computer since.

events.title: Migrant Mother
events.body: Dorothea Lange photographs Florence Owens Thompson, a pea-picker in California, and her children. It becomes the face of the Depression.

events.title: The Spanish Civil War
events.body: General Franco leads an army uprising against Spain's elected Republic. The war draws in Hitler and Mussolini on one side and volunteers from around the world on the other.

events.title: Jesse Owens in Berlin
events.body: At the Nazi Olympics, Black American sprinter Jesse Owens wins four gold medals.

events.title: The Bombing of Guernica
events.body: German and Italian aircraft bomb the Basque town of Guernica on market day, for Franco. It becomes a symbol of the terror bombing of civilians.

events.title: The Hindenburg Disaster
events.body: The German airship bursts into flames while landing in New Jersey, killing 36. The age of the passenger airship ends.

events.title: Guernica
events.body: Picasso paints a huge black, white and grey canvas of screaming people and animals for the Spanish pavilion at the Paris World's Fair.

events.title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
events.body: Zora Neale Hurston's novel follows Janie Crawford's search for her own voice in the Black towns of Florida.

events.title: The Great Terror
events.body: Stalin's purges reach their peak. In 1937 and 1938, by the secret police's own records, about 680,000 people are shot and many more sent to the Gulag.

events.title: Amelia Earhart Disappears
events.body: Pioneering aviator Amelia Earhart vanishes over the Pacific while trying to fly around the world.

events.title: The Parsley Massacre
events.body: Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo's soldiers kill thousands of Haitians and Dominicans of Haitian descent along the border; estimates range widely.

events.title: The Nanjing Massacre
events.body: Japanese troops take the Chinese capital Nanjing and, over six weeks, kill tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of civilians and prisoners and rape tens of thousands of women.

events.title: Mexico Nationalises Its Oil
events.body: President Lázaro Cárdenas takes over the foreign oil companies operating in Mexico, creating Pemex. Mexicans line up to donate to pay compensation.

events.title: The Jamaica Labour Rebellion
events.body: Strikes at the Frome sugar estate spread across Jamaica, part of a wave of labour revolts in the Caribbean. Trade unions and the parties that later lead independence grow out of them.

events.title: The Munich Agreement
events.body: Britain and France let Hitler take part of Czechoslovakia. Chamberlain promises 'peace for our time'. Within a year Europe is at war.

events.title: The War of the Worlds Broadcast
events.body: Orson Welles's radio drama of a Martian invasion, told as news bulletins, frightens some listeners into thinking it is real.

events.title: Kristallnacht
events.body: Nazis attack Jewish homes, shops and synagogues across Germany and Austria in a night of violence. About 30,000 Jewish men are sent to concentration camps.

events.title: Nuclear Fission
events.body: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann split the uranium atom in Berlin; Lise Meitner, a Jewish exile in Sweden, and her nephew explain what has happened.

events.title: The Great Trek Centenary
events.body: Afrikaner nationalists re-enact the Great Trek with ox-wagons converging on Pretoria for the laying of the Voortrekker Monument's foundation stone — a surge of feeling the National Party will ride to power.

events.title: The Grapes of Wrath
events.body: John Steinbeck's novel follows the Joad family from the Dust Bowl to California. It is banned and burned in some places — and wins the Pulitzer Prize.

events.title: Strange Fruit
events.body: Billie Holiday records 'Strange Fruit', a song about lynching in the American South, which her record label had refused to touch.

events.title: Mbube
events.body: Solomon Linda and the Evening Birds record 'Mbube' in Johannesburg. It becomes 'The Lion Sleeps Tonight', earning millions — while Linda dies poor.

events.title: Germany Invades Poland
events.body: Germany invades Poland. Britain and France declare war two days later; the Soviet Union invades from the east on 17 September. The Second World War has begun.

sources.title: Allies at War with Germany (4 September 1939)

events.title: Gone with the Wind
events.body: The Civil War epic premieres in Atlanta. Hattie McDaniel becomes the first Black actor to win an Oscar — but is barred from the premiere by segregation.

events.title: Rationing in Britain
events.body: Britain rations bacon, butter and sugar; meat, tea and much else follow. Rationing does not fully end until 1954.

events.title: Dunkirk
events.body: Over nine days, warships, ferries and small boats rescue more than 330,000 British and French soldiers trapped on the beaches of Dunkirk.

sources.title: We Shall Fight on the Beaches (4 June 1940)

events.title: De Gaulle's Appeal
events.body: With France about to surrender, General de Gaulle broadcasts from London on the BBC, calling on the French to fight on. The Free French movement is born.

events.title: Chad Joins Free France
events.body: Governor Félix Éboué, born in French Guiana, takes Chad over to de Gaulle — the first French colony to do so.

events.title: The Blitz
events.body: The German air force begins bombing London night after night for eight months; Coventry, Liverpool and other cities are hit too. Over 40,000 British civilians die.

events.title: Citizen Kane
events.body: Orson Welles's first film, about a newspaper tycoon, premieres in New York. It is often voted the greatest film ever made.

events.title: Germany Invades the Soviet Union
events.body: Over three million German and allied troops pour into the Soviet Union in Operation Barbarossa — the largest invasion in history. Behind the lines, mass shootings of Jews begin.

events.title: The Siege of Leningrad
events.body: German and Finnish forces encircle Leningrad. The siege lasts almost 900 days; around a million civilians die, most of them from starvation.

events.title: Pearl Harbor
events.body: Japan attacks the American fleet at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii and, within hours, British and American territories across Asia. The United States enters the war.

events.title: The Wannsee Conference
events.body: Senior Nazi officials meet in a villa outside Berlin to coordinate the 'Final Solution' — the murder of Europe's Jews.

events.title: Darwin Bombed
events.body: Japanese aircraft — many from the carriers that struck Pearl Harbor — attack Darwin, killing more than 230 people. It is the first of many raids on northern Australia.

events.title: The Battle of Midway
events.body: American carrier aircraft sink four Japanese carriers in a single day. The war in the Pacific turns.

events.title: Lidice Destroyed
events.body: In revenge for the assassination of SS leader Reinhard Heydrich, the Nazis shoot the men of the Czech village of Lidice, deport its women and children, and raze it.

events.title: Guadalcanal
events.body: US Marines land on Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands. Six months of fighting follow; Solomon Islander scouts play a vital part.

events.title: El Alamein
events.body: In the Egyptian desert, the Eighth Army — British, Australian, New Zealand, Indian, South African, Free French and Greek troops — defeats Rommel's Axis army.

events.title: Stalingrad
events.body: The surrounded German Sixth Army surrenders at Stalingrad after five months of fighting street by street. Nearly two million soldiers and civilians have been killed, wounded or captured; the tide in Europe turns.

events.title: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
events.body: Jewish fighters in the Warsaw Ghetto rise against the Nazis as deportations to Treblinka resume. They hold out for nearly a month.

events.title: The Bengal Famine
events.body: Famine kills an estimated two to three million people in British-ruled Bengal, made worse by wartime policy and the failure to send help.

events.title: Peoples Deported to Central Asia
events.body: Stalin deports the whole Chechen and Ingush peoples to Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan in cattle wagons; the Crimean Tatars follow in May. Many die on the way and in the first years of exile.

events.title: D-Day
events.body: Allied forces land on five beaches in Normandy — the largest seaborne invasion in history — opening a second front in Western Europe.

events.title: Saipan
events.body: US forces invade Saipan. As the island falls, hundreds of Japanese civilians kill themselves rather than surrender; its airfields put Japan within reach of American bombers.

events.title: Bretton Woods
events.body: Allied countries meet in New Hampshire to plan the post-war economy, creating the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank and tying currencies to the dollar.

events.title: Colossus Breaks Codes
events.body: At Bletchley Park, the Colossus machines — the first programmable electronic digital computers — help break German high-command codes, building on Turing's work.

events.title: Anne Frank Arrested
events.body: After two years hiding in a secret annexe in Amsterdam, Anne Frank and her family are betrayed and arrested. Anne dies in Bergen-Belsen months later, aged 15.

events.title: Auschwitz Liberated
events.body: Soviet soldiers reach Auschwitz-Birkenau, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered. Six million Jews died in the Holocaust, along with Roma, disabled people and many others.

events.title: The Yalta Conference
events.body: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin meet in Crimea to plan the end of the war and the shape of post-war Europe, including Soviet control over Eastern Europe.

events.title: Victory in Europe
events.body: Germany surrenders unconditionally, a week after Hitler kills himself in Berlin. Crowds celebrate across Europe.

events.title: The Sétif Massacre
events.body: On the same day as Victory in Europe celebrations, Algerian protests for independence in Sétif are met with French massacres that kill thousands of Algerians.

events.title: The United Nations Charter
events.body: Fifty countries sign the United Nations Charter in San Francisco, replacing the failed League of Nations.

events.title: The Trinity Test
events.body: The first atomic bomb is exploded in the New Mexico desert. Oppenheimer later recalls the words: 'Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.'

events.title: Hiroshima
events.body: An American B-29 drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, killing tens of thousands instantly and many more from burns and radiation. Nagasaki follows three days later.

sources.title: Truman's statement announcing the bombing of Hiroshima
The Atomic Bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

events.title: Japan Surrenders
events.body: Emperor Hirohito broadcasts Japan's surrender to his people, the first time most of them have heard his voice. The Second World War ends.

events.title: Indonesia Declares Independence
events.body: Sukarno proclaims Indonesia's independence from the Netherlands, two days after Japan's surrender. Four years of war with the Dutch follow.

events.title: Animal Farm
events.body: George Orwell's fable of farm animals whose revolution is betrayed by the pigs — an attack on Stalin's Soviet Union — is published in London.

events.title: Vietnam Declares Independence
events.body: In Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh reads a declaration of independence that quotes America's own. France will fight to keep its colony.

events.title: The Manchester Pan-African Congress
events.body: Kwame Nkrumah, Jomo Kenyatta, W. E. B. Du Bois and others meet in Manchester and demand independence for Africa — the start of the end of empire on the continent.

events.title: The Nuremberg Trials
events.body: Surviving Nazi leaders go on trial before an international court, charged with crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

events.title: ENIAC
events.body: The first general-purpose electronic computer is unveiled in Philadelphia. It fills a room and weighs about 27 tonnes.

events.title: Perón Elected
events.body: Juan Perón, a colonel popular with workers, is elected president of Argentina. Peronism shapes Argentine politics to this day.

events.title: The Iron Curtain
events.body: In a speech at Fulton, Missouri, Churchill says 'an iron curtain has descended across the Continent'. The Cold War has a name for its divide.

sources.title: The Sinews of Peace ('Iron Curtain' speech)

events.title: Nuclear Tests at Bikini
events.body: The United States begins nuclear tests at Bikini Atoll in the Pacific, after moving its people off the island. They have never been able to return to live there safely.

events.title: The Philippines Becomes Independent
events.body: After nearly fifty years of American rule and Japanese occupation in the war, the Philippines becomes independent.

events.title: The Bikini
events.body: Louis Réard shows a two-piece swimsuit in Paris and names it after the atoll where the bomb tests have just begun.

events.title: The African Mine Workers' Strike
events.body: Around 70,000 Black mine workers on the Witwatersrand strike for better wages. Police break the strike, killing at least nine.

events.title: Dior's New Look
events.body: Christian Dior's first collection, with nipped waists and full skirts using metres of fabric, ends wartime austerity in fashion.

events.title: The February 28 Incident
events.body: A clash over contraband cigarettes in Taipei sparks an island-wide uprising against the Nationalist government. Troops kill thousands. Martial law, declared two years later, lasts until 1987.

events.title: The Malagasy Uprising
events.body: Malagasy nationalists rise against French rule in Madagascar. French forces put it down over nearly two years; tens of thousands die.

events.title: Jackie Robinson Breaks the Colour Line
events.body: Jackie Robinson plays first base for the Brooklyn Dodgers, the first Black player in Major League Baseball in the modern era.

events.title: The Diary of Anne Frank Published
events.body: Otto Frank, the only member of the family to survive, publishes his daughter's diary in Amsterdam. It becomes one of the most read books in the world.

events.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
events.body: Bedouin shepherds find ancient scrolls in caves at Qumran. They include the oldest known copies of books of the Hebrew Bible.

events.title: If This Is a Man
events.body: Italian chemist Primo Levi publishes his account of surviving Auschwitz, written with a scientist's clarity.

events.title: Independence and Partition
events.body: British India becomes independent as two countries, India and Pakistan. The partition sets off mass migration and killing: some 15 million people are uprooted, and estimates of the dead range from hundreds of thousands to two million.

events.title: The Dakar–Niger Railway Strike
events.body: African railway workers across French West Africa strike for more than five months for the same pay and benefits as Europeans, and win many of their demands.

events.title: A Streetcar Named Desire
events.body: Tennessee Williams's play, with Marlon Brando as Stanley Kowalski, opens on Broadway.

events.title: The Transistor
events.body: At Bell Labs in New Jersey, three physicists demonstrate the first transistor — the tiny switch inside every modern electronic device.

events.title: Burma Becomes Independent
events.body: Burma leaves the British Empire as an independent republic, months after its independence leader Aung San is assassinated.

events.title: Gandhi Assassinated
events.body: A Hindu nationalist shoots Mahatma Gandhi at a prayer meeting in Delhi, five months after independence.

events.title: The Accra Riots
events.body: Police fire on African ex-servicemen marching to the governor's castle with a petition, killing three. Riots follow, and the path to independence speeds up.

events.title: The Bogotazo
events.body: The murder of popular Liberal leader Jorge Eliécer Gaitán sets off riots that destroy much of central Bogotá and open a decade of violence in Colombia.

events.title: Israel Founded — the Nakba
events.body: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel. In the war that follows, some 700,000 Palestinians flee or are expelled — the Nakba, or 'catastrophe'.

events.title: Apartheid Wins the Election
events.body: D. F. Malan's National Party wins South Africa's whites-only election on a platform of apartheid — strict racial separation written into law.

sources.title: 26 May 1948: the day that changed South Africa forever

events.title: The Empire Windrush
events.body: The ship Empire Windrush docks at Tilbury carrying hundreds of people from the Caribbean invited to help rebuild Britain.

events.title: The Berlin Airlift
events.body: The Soviet Union blockades West Berlin. For almost a year, American and British aircraft fly in food and coal, at times landing every few minutes.

events.title: Bicycle Thieves
events.body: Vittorio De Sica's film of a poor man in post-war Rome searching for his stolen bicycle, cast with non-actors, becomes the heart of Italian neorealism.

events.title: Cry, the Beloved Country
events.body: Alan Paton's novel of a Zulu priest searching for his son in Johannesburg is published the year apartheid comes to power, and introduces South Africa's racial injustice to readers abroad.

events.title: The NHS Is Born
events.body: Britain's National Health Service opens, offering medical care free to everyone at the point of use.

events.title: Costa Rica Abolishes Its Army
events.body: After a short civil war, José Figueres takes a sledgehammer to a barracks wall and abolishes Costa Rica's army. Its money goes to schools and health care.

events.title: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
events.body: The UN General Assembly in Paris adopts a declaration of rights belonging to every person, drafted by a committee chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt. South Africa abstains.

events.title: NATO Founded
events.body: Twelve countries in North America and Western Europe sign a treaty in Washington promising to defend each other.

events.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
events.body: George Orwell's novel of a totalitarian state that watches everyone, rewrites history and controls thought gives the world 'Big Brother'.

events.title: The Second Sex
events.body: Simone de Beauvoir's study of how women have been made 'the Other' — 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' — becomes a founding text of modern feminism.

events.title: The Mixed Marriages Act
events.body: South Africa's first major apartheid law bans marriage between white people and people of other races.

events.title: The Soviet Bomb
events.body: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb in Kazakhstan, years earlier than the West expected. The nuclear arms race begins.

events.title: The People's Republic of China
events.body: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China in Beijing. Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists retreat to Taiwan.

sources.title: Proclamation of the Central People's Government (1 October 1949)

events.title: The Korean War Begins
events.body: North Korean forces invade the South. A US-led UN force and, later, Chinese troops join a war that kills millions and ends without a peace treaty.

events.title: The Population Registration Act
events.body: Apartheid South Africa classifies every person by race. The Group Areas Act the same year decides where each 'race' may live, work and own property.

sources.title: Population Registration Act, Act No 30 of 1950

events.title: The HeLa Cells
events.body: Cells taken without consent from Henrietta Lacks, a Black woman dying of cancer in Baltimore, become the first human cells to keep growing in a lab — used in research ever since.

events.title: A New Queen
events.body: George VI dies in his sleep; his daughter Elizabeth, on a tour of Kenya, becomes queen. She will reign for seventy years.

events.title: The Bolivian Revolution
events.body: Miners and townspeople bring the MNR to power in Bolivia. The vote is opened to all adults, the tin mines are nationalised and land is redistributed.

events.title: The Defiance Campaign
events.body: The ANC and its allies launch a campaign of deliberately breaking apartheid laws. More than 8,000 volunteers are arrested.

events.title: Egypt's Revolution
events.body: The Free Officers, led by Mohamed Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser, overthrow King Farouk. Egypt becomes a republic the next year.

events.title: Evita Dies
events.body: Eva Perón, champion of Argentina's poor and of women's suffrage, dies of cancer at 33. Millions mourn her.

events.title: The Mau Mau Emergency
events.body: Britain declares a state of emergency in Kenya against the Mau Mau rebellion. Tens of thousands of Kenyans are detained in camps, many tortured.

events.title: The Great Smog
events.body: A cold, windless fog traps coal smoke over London for five days. About 4,000 people die at the time; later estimates are much higher. It leads to the Clean Air Act of 1956.

events.title: Waiting for Godot
events.body: Samuel Beckett's play, in which two tramps wait for someone who never comes, premieres in Paris. Theatre is never quite the same.

events.title: Stalin Dies
events.body: Joseph Stalin dies after nearly thirty years ruling the Soviet Union. Three years later, Khrushchev denounces his crimes in a secret speech.

events.title: The Double Helix
events.body: Watson and Crick publish the structure of DNA in Nature, built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image, Photo 51, which they saw without her knowledge.

events.title: The Summit of Everest
events.body: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary become the first climbers known to reach the top of Mount Everest.

events.title: The Korean Armistice
events.body: An armistice signed at Panmunjom ends the fighting in Korea, leaving the peninsula divided along almost the same line as before.

events.title: The Coup in Iran
events.body: A coup backed by the CIA and British intelligence overthrows Iran's elected prime minister, Mohammad Mosaddegh, who had nationalised the oil industry, and restores the Shah's power.

events.title: The Four-Minute Mile
events.body: Medical student Roger Bannister runs a mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds at Iffley Road, Oxford — a barrier many thought impossible.

events.title: Điện Biên Phủ
events.body: Vietnamese forces under General Giáp overwhelm the French garrison at Điện Biên Phủ. France leaves Indochina; Vietnam is divided in two.

events.title: Brown v. Board of Education
events.body: The US Supreme Court rules that racially segregated public schools are unconstitutional.

events.title: The Guatemalan Coup
events.body: A CIA-backed invasion forces out President Jacobo Árbenz, whose land reform had taken unused land from the United Fruit Company. A young Che Guevara is in Guatemala City and sees it happen.

events.title: Seven Samurai
events.body: Akira Kurosawa's epic of villagers hiring masterless samurai to defend them is released, and goes on to shape action films around the world.

events.title: The Virgin Lands Campaign
events.body: Khrushchev sends hundreds of thousands of young Soviet volunteers to plough the steppe of northern Kazakhstan for wheat.

events.title: The Algerian War Begins
events.body: The National Liberation Front launches attacks across Algeria. Eight years of war follow, with torture and atrocities on both sides, before independence.

events.title: Sophiatown Destroyed
events.body: Armed police begin forcibly removing residents of Sophiatown, Johannesburg's vibrant mixed suburb of jazz and writers. It is bulldozed and rebuilt as a white suburb named Triomf.

events.title: The Polio Vaccine
events.body: Jonas Salk's vaccine against polio is declared safe and effective. Salk refuses to patent it.

events.title: The Bandung Conference
events.body: Leaders from 29 African and Asian countries meet in Bandung, Indonesia — the first great gathering of the newly independent world, and the seed of the Non-Aligned Movement.

events.title: The Freedom Charter
events.body: At the Congress of the People in Kliptown, thousands adopt the Freedom Charter: 'South Africa belongs to all who live in it, black and white.'

sources.title: The Freedom Charter, adopted at Kliptown, 25–26 June 1955

events.title: Pather Panchali
events.body: Satyajit Ray's first film, about a poor family in a Bengali village, made on a shoestring over three years, announces Indian art cinema to the world.

events.title: Emmett Till Murdered
events.body: Fourteen-year-old Emmett Till is abducted and murdered in Mississippi. His mother insists on an open casket so the world can see what was done to him.

events.title: Rosa Parks Stays Seated
events.body: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her seat to a white passenger on a Montgomery bus. The 381-day bus boycott that follows makes Martin Luther King Jr. a national leader.

events.title: Sudan Becomes Independent
events.body: Sudan becomes independent from British and Egyptian rule.

events.title: Heartbreak Hotel
events.body: Elvis Presley's first national hit is released, and rock and roll — born from Black rhythm and blues and gospel — goes mainstream.

events.title: Morocco and Tunisia Become Independent
events.body: France recognises Morocco's independence on 2 March and Tunisia's on 20 March.

events.title: The Suez Crisis
events.body: Egypt's President Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal. Britain, France and Israel invade in October but are forced to withdraw under US and Soviet pressure — the end of Britain as a superpower.

events.title: The Women's March to Pretoria
events.body: Some 20,000 women of all races march on the Union Buildings against pass laws, singing 'wathint' abafazi, wathint' imbokodo' — you strike a woman, you strike a rock.

events.title: Maralinga
events.body: Britain begins nuclear weapons tests at Maralinga in South Australia. Aboriginal people living on the land are exposed to fallout.

events.title: The Hungarian Uprising
events.body: Students and workers in Budapest rise against Soviet rule. Soviet tanks crush the revolution within weeks; about 200,000 Hungarians flee.

events.title: The Treason Trial
events.body: 156 leaders of the Congress Alliance, including Mandela and Albert Luthuli, are arrested for treason. The trial drags on for over four years; all are acquitted.

events.title: Ghana Becomes Independent
events.body: Gold Coast becomes Ghana, the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence. Kwame Nkrumah declares 'Ghana, your beloved country, is free for ever.'

events.title: The Treaty of Rome
events.body: Six countries sign the treaty founding the European Economic Community, the forerunner of the European Union.

events.title: Mother India
events.body: Mehboob Khan's epic of a poor village woman, played by Nargis, becomes the first Indian film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

events.title: The Little Rock Nine
events.body: Nine Black students try to enter Little Rock Central High School and are blocked by the Arkansas National Guard. President Eisenhower sends troops to escort them in.

events.title: West Side Story
events.body: Romeo and Juliet moves to the gang streets of New York's Upper West Side, with music by Leonard Bernstein and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim.

events.title: Sputnik
events.body: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik, the first artificial satellite. Its beeping signal, heard by radios worldwide, starts the space race.

events.title: Laika in Orbit
events.body: A stray dog from Moscow's streets, Laika, becomes the first animal to orbit the Earth. She dies within hours from overheating.

events.title: The Keeling Curve
events.body: Charles David Keeling begins measuring carbon dioxide on Mauna Loa in Hawaii. His record, still running, shows the level rising every year.

events.title: China's Great Leap Forward
events.body: Mao launches a campaign to industrialise China at speed through communes and backyard furnaces. The famine that follows kills tens of millions.

events.title: Pelé's World Cup
events.body: Seventeen-year-old Pelé scores twice as Brazil beat hosts Sweden 5–2 to win their first World Cup.

events.title: Things Fall Apart
events.body: Chinua Achebe's novel of Okonkwo, an Igbo leader whose world is undone by colonialism and missionaries, becomes the most widely read African novel.

events.title: Iraq's Revolution
events.body: Army officers overthrow Iraq's monarchy; the young king and much of the royal family are killed.

events.title: Instant Noodles
events.body: Momofuku Ando, working in a shed in his garden near Osaka, launches Chikin Ramen, the first instant noodles.

events.title: The Integrated Circuit
events.body: Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments shows the first working integrated circuit — several components on one piece of semiconductor. The microchip follows.

events.title: Guinea Says No
events.body: Guinea is the only French colony to vote No in de Gaulle's referendum on a new French Community. It becomes independent days later, and France pulls out overnight.

events.title: The Cuban Revolution
events.body: Dictator Fulgencio Batista flees Cuba. Fidel Castro and Che Guevara's rebels take Havana.

events.title: The Léopoldville Riots
events.body: After a banned political meeting, riots break out in the Congo's capital; dozens are killed. Within days, Belgium promises independence.

events.title: Barbie
events.body: Mattel introduces Barbie at the New York Toy Fair, an adult-looking doll designed by Ruth Handler, who named her after her daughter.

events.title: The Dalai Lama Flees
events.body: After a failed uprising against Chinese rule in Lhasa, the young Dalai Lama escapes over the Himalayas to exile in India.

events.title: The PAC Breaks Away
events.body: Robert Sobukwe leads Africanists out of the ANC to form the Pan Africanist Congress. Within a year its anti-pass campaign leads to Sharpeville.

events.title: Kind of Blue
events.body: Miles Davis's quiet, modal jazz album, made in two sessions with little rehearsal, becomes the best-selling jazz record of all time.

events.title: The Wind of Change
events.body: In Cape Town's parliament, British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan says 'the wind of change is blowing through this continent', signalling Britain's retreat from empire in Africa.

events.title: The Sharpeville Massacre
events.body: Police open fire on a crowd protesting against pass laws outside Sharpeville police station, killing 69 people, many shot in the back. The ANC and PAC are banned and turn to armed struggle.

events.title: Brasília Inaugurated
events.body: Brazil moves its capital to a new city built in under four years in the interior, planned by Lúcio Costa with buildings by Oscar Niemeyer.

events.title: The Pill Approved
events.body: The US Food and Drug Administration approves the first oral contraceptive pill, giving women new control over whether and when to have children.

events.title: The First Laser
events.body: Theodore Maiman makes the first working laser at Hughes Research Laboratories in California, using a ruby crystal.

events.title: The Valdivia Earthquake
events.body: The most powerful earthquake ever recorded, magnitude 9.5, strikes southern Chile. Its tsunami kills people as far away as Hawaii and Japan.

events.title: The Year of Africa
events.body: In 1960, seventeen African countries become independent. In the Congo, Patrice Lumumba's independence-day speech condemns Belgian rule to the Belgian king's face.

events.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
events.body: Harper Lee's novel of a Black man falsely accused of rape in 1930s Alabama, seen through a young girl's eyes, is published to instant success.

events.title: God's Bits of Wood
events.body: Ousmane Sembène, a former docker, publishes his novel of the railway strike and the women who sustained it.

events.title: The Aral Sea Begins to Die
events.body: Soviet planners divert the rivers feeding the Aral Sea to irrigate cotton. Once one of the world's largest lakes, it shrinks to a fraction of its size, leaving a salty desert.

events.title: Lumumba Murdered
events.body: Congo's first prime minister is executed by Katangan separatists with Belgian involvement, after the CIA had also plotted his death. Mobutu rises to power.

events.title: Angola's War of Independence
events.body: Nationalists attack Luanda's prison. The war against Portuguese rule lasts thirteen years.

events.title: Gagarin Orbits the Earth
events.body: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space, circling the Earth once in 108 minutes in Vostok 1.

events.title: The Bay of Pigs
events.body: A CIA-trained force of Cuban exiles lands at the Bay of Pigs to overthrow Castro and is defeated within three days.

events.title: Amnesty International Founded
events.body: A London lawyer's newspaper appeal for 'the forgotten prisoners' — people jailed for their beliefs — grows into Amnesty International.

events.title: South Africa Becomes a Republic
events.body: South Africa leaves the Commonwealth and becomes a republic after a whites-only referendum.

events.title: The Berlin Wall Goes Up
events.body: Overnight, East Germany seals the border through Berlin with barbed wire, soon replaced by a concrete wall. Families are split for 28 years.

events.title: A Nobel for Albert Luthuli
events.body: ANC president Albert Luthuli receives the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo for his non-violent struggle against apartheid — the first African to win it.

events.title: Umkhonto we Sizwe
events.body: The ANC's new armed wing, Umkhonto we Sizwe, sets off its first bombs at government buildings, avoiding loss of life.

events.title: Samoa Becomes Independent
events.body: Western Samoa becomes the first Pacific island nation to regain independence in the 20th century.

events.title: Warhol's Soup Cans
events.body: Andy Warhol shows 32 paintings of Campbell's soup cans in Los Angeles. Pop art makes the mass-produced everyday into art.

events.title: Spacewar!
events.body: Programmers at MIT write Spacewar!, two spaceships duelling around a star — one of the first video games, copied onto computers across America.

events.title: Algeria Becomes Independent
events.body: After eight years of war and more than a century of French rule, Algeria becomes independent.

events.title: Mandela Arrested
events.body: Nelson Mandela, underground for over a year, is arrested near Howick in Natal. Eleven months later, police raid Liliesleaf farm in Rivonia and arrest his comrades.

events.title: Jamaica and Trinidad Become Independent
events.body: Jamaica becomes independent on 6 August; Trinidad and Tobago follows on 31 August.

events.title: Silent Spring
events.body: Rachel Carson's book shows how pesticides like DDT poison birds, fish and people. It launches the modern environmental movement.

events.title: Love Me Do
events.body: The Beatles release their first single in Britain. Within two years, Beatlemania sweeps the world.

events.title: The Second Vatican Council
events.body: Pope John XXIII opens the council that will modernise the Catholic Church, allowing Mass in local languages instead of Latin.

events.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis
events.body: US spy planes find Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba. For thirteen days the world comes closer to nuclear war than ever before, until Khrushchev agrees to remove them.

events.title: The Sino-Indian War
events.body: China attacks along the disputed Himalayan border with India. After a month of fighting, China declares a ceasefire and holds Aksai Chin.

events.title: The Organisation of African Unity
events.body: Leaders of 32 independent African states meet in Addis Ababa to found the Organisation of African Unity.

events.title: The First Woman in Space
events.body: Valentina Tereshkova, a textile worker and amateur parachutist, orbits the Earth 48 times in Vostok 6.

events.title: The Feminine Mystique
events.body: Betty Friedan writes about 'the problem that has no name' — the unhappiness of American housewives — and helps spark second-wave feminism.

events.title: I Have a Dream
events.body: At the March on Washington, before about 250,000 people, Martin Luther King Jr. speaks of his dream of a nation where his children are judged 'by the content of their character'.

sources.title: Official Program for the March on Washington

events.title: Kennedy Assassinated
events.body: President John F. Kennedy is shot dead while riding in an open car through Dallas.

events.title: Kenya Becomes Independent
events.body: Kenya becomes independent from Britain. Jomo Kenyatta, once jailed by the colonial government as a supposed Mau Mau leader, becomes prime minister.

events.title: Cassius Clay Shocks the World
events.body: Twenty-two-year-old Cassius Clay beats Sonny Liston to become heavyweight champion — and soon announces his new name, Muhammad Ali.

events.title: The Brazilian Coup
events.body: The military overthrows President João Goulart, with US backing, beginning 21 years of dictatorship in Brazil.

events.title: The Rivonia Trial Verdict
events.body: Nelson Mandela and seven others are sentenced to life imprisonment. In court, Mandela says the ideal of a democratic and free society is one 'for which I am prepared to die'.

events.title: Mississippi Goddam
events.body: Nina Simone writes 'Mississippi Goddam' in under an hour after the murder of Medgar Evers and the Birmingham church bombing. It becomes a civil rights anthem.

events.title: Weep Not, Child
events.body: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o's first novel, about a Kikuyu boy's dreams of education during the Mau Mau emergency, is the first English-language novel by an East African writer.

events.title: The Civil Rights Act
events.body: President Johnson signs a law outlawing discrimination by race, colour, religion, sex or national origin in the United States.

events.title: The Bullet Train
events.body: Japan opens the Tōkaidō Shinkansen between Tokyo and Osaka, the world's first high-speed railway, days before the Tokyo Olympics.

events.title: Malcolm X Assassinated
events.body: Malcolm X is shot dead as he begins a speech at the Audubon Ballroom in Manhattan, a year after breaking with the Nation of Islam.

events.title: Bloody Sunday at Selma
events.body: State troopers beat peaceful marchers on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama. Televised, it pushes Congress to pass the Voting Rights Act.

events.title: US Combat Troops in Vietnam
events.body: The first American combat troops land at Da Nang. By 1968 more than half a million are in Vietnam.

events.title: The Indonesian Killings
events.body: After an attempted coup, the Indonesian army and allied militias kill hundreds of thousands of suspected communists over the following months. Suharto takes power.

events.title: Rhodesia's UDI
events.body: Ian Smith's white minority government declares independence from Britain to prevent Black majority rule. A long liberation war follows.

events.title: Mobutu Takes Power
events.body: Army chief Joseph-Désiré Mobutu seizes power in the Congo. He rules for 32 years and renames the country Zaire.

events.title: Indira Gandhi Becomes Prime Minister
events.body: Indira Gandhi becomes India's first woman prime minister.

events.title: District Six Declared White
events.body: The apartheid government declares Cape Town's District Six a white area. Over the next fifteen years some 60,000 residents are forced out and their homes bulldozed.

events.title: The Cultural Revolution
events.body: Mao launches a campaign against 'bourgeois' elements. Red Guards attack teachers, officials and temples. Estimates of the dead over the next decade range from hundreds of thousands to about two million.

events.title: Nuclear Tests at Moruroa
events.body: France sets off its first atomic bomb at Moruroa atoll in French Polynesia. Nearly 200 tests follow over thirty years.

events.title: England Win the World Cup
events.body: England beat West Germany 4–2 after extra time at Wembley, with a hat-trick from Geoff Hurst. Eusébio of Portugal, born in Mozambique, is the tournament's top scorer.

events.title: Verwoerd Assassinated
events.body: The architect of apartheid is stabbed to death in parliament by a parliamentary messenger, Dimitri Tsafendas.

events.title: Aberfan
events.body: A colliery spoil tip slides down onto a village school in Wales, killing 116 children and 28 adults.

events.title: The 1967 Referendum
events.body: More than 90 per cent of Australian voters agree to count Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in the census and let the federal government make laws for them.

events.title: The Nigerian Civil War
events.body: The Eastern Region declares itself the Republic of Biafra. In the war that follows, a blockade causes famine; estimates of civilian deaths, mostly from starvation, range from about half a million to two million.

events.title: The Six-Day War
