events.body: Soviet physicist and human rights activist Andrei Sakharov is released from seven years of internal exile under Gorbachev's glasnost policy. His release is a powerful signal of genuine change in the Soviet Union.

events.title: Voyager Completes Round-the-World Flight
events.body: The experimental aircraft Voyager, piloted by Dick Rutan and Jeana Yeager, completes the first non-stop, non-refuelled circumnavigation of the Earth in approximately 9 days, landing with less than 18 litres of fuel remaining.

events.title: Andy Warhol Dies
events.body: The king of Pop Art dies unexpectedly at 58 after gallbladder surgery in New York. His estate funds a foundation that still shapes contemporary art.

events.title: Supernova 1987A
events.body: Light from an exploding star in the Large Magellanic Cloud reaches Earth — the nearest observed supernova in 383 years, and a bonanza for astronomy.

events.title: Zeebrugge Disaster
events.body: The ferry Herald of Free Enterprise capsizes moments after leaving port with her bow doors open; 193 passengers and crew die.

events.title: The Joshua Tree Released
events.body: U2's album of wide-open American spaces — With or Without You, Where the Streets Have No Name — makes them the biggest band in the world.

events.title: Sunflowers Sells for a Record
events.body: Van Gogh's Sunflowers fetches £24.75 million at Christie's — nearly quadruple the previous record for any painting, igniting the 1980s art boom.

events.title: Red Bull Launches
events.body: An Austrian entrepreneur adapts a Thai tonic and invents the energy-drink category. Within decades it sells billions of cans and owns football teams and Formula 1 outfits.

events.title: Diana Shakes Hands Without Gloves
events.body: Opening Britain's first dedicated AIDS ward, the Princess of Wales shakes patients' hands bare-handed — a simple gesture that helps dismantle public fear.

events.title: The Simpsons First Appear
events.body: Springfield's family debuts as crude shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show — the seed of television's longest-running scripted series.

events.title: Fiji's First Coup
events.body: Lieutenant-Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka overthrows Fiji's newly elected, mainly Indo-Fijian-backed government. A second coup follows in September.

events.title: Iraqi Missiles Hit USS Stark
events.body: An Iraqi jet fires two Exocets into the American frigate in the Gulf, killing 37 sailors — the deadliest attack on a US warship since the Second World War.

events.title: Thatcher Wins a Third Term
events.body: The Conservatives take a 102-seat majority — making Thatcher the first British PM in modern times to win three consecutive elections.

events.title: "Tear Down This Wall!"
events.body: At the Brandenburg Gate, Reagan challenges Gorbachev to demolish the Berlin Wall. The line barely registers at the time — and echoes through history two years later.

events.title: All Blacks Win the First Rugby World Cup
events.body: New Zealand beat France 29–9 at Eden Park in the inaugural tournament — one South Africa, excluded under apartheid, can only watch.

events.title: Silence = Death
events.body: A pink triangle on black and three words fly-posted across Manhattan by a small activist collective. Adopted by ACT UP, it becomes the defining image of AIDS activism.

events.title: Sarafina!
events.body: Mbongeni Ngema's musical about schoolchildren in the Soweto uprising opens at the Market Theatre, then on Broadway. Its young cast sings mbaqanga and gospel about guns and classrooms.

events.title: “Beds Are Burning”
events.body: Midnight Oil's demand that Australia “pay the rent” and give the land back to its first peoples, written after the band toured remote Aboriginal communities. It lands just as the country prepares to celebrate 200 years of settlement.

events.title: “Bring Him Back Home”
events.body: Exiled trumpeter Hugh Masekela's song imagining Nelson Mandela “walking hand in hand with Winnie” down the streets of Soweto. He plays it at the Wembley birthday concert.

events.title: And the Band Played On
events.body: Journalist Randy Shilts's history of the first years of the AIDS epidemic — and of how government, science and the media failed to respond while thousands died.

events.title: Five Billion People
events.body: The UN designates a Yugoslav baby the symbolic five-billionth human. World population has doubled since 1950.

events.title: Appetite for Destruction Released
events.body: Guns N' Roses' debut sells slowly, then explodes — eventually the best-selling debut album in American history.

events.title: Never Gonna Give You Up
events.body: Rick Astley's debut single tops charts in 25 countries. Two decades later the internet reinvents it as the "rickroll".

events.title: Hungerford Massacre
events.body: A gunman kills 16 people in a Berkshire market town before shooting himself. Britain bans semi-automatic rifles in response.

events.title: Dirty Dancing Opens
events.body: A low-budget dance romance becomes a word-of-mouth phenomenon — and nobody puts Baby in a corner.

events.title: The Montreal Protocol
events.body: Nations agree to phase out the CFCs destroying the ozone layer — still the most successful environmental treaty ever signed, and the ozone hole is now healing.

events.title: The AIDS Memorial Quilt
events.body: 1,920 panels, each sewn for someone lost to AIDS, are laid out on the National Mall in Washington. Begun by activist Cleve Jones, the quilt grows into the largest piece of community folk art in the world.

events.title: The Great Storm
events.body: Hurricane-force winds flatten some 15 million trees across southern England overnight — hours after the BBC's Michael Fish reassured viewers there was no hurricane coming.

events.title: “They Dance Alone”
events.body: Sting's song for the women of Chile who dance the cueca alone, holding photographs of their disappeared partners. He later sings it in Chile with the mothers dancing on stage.

events.title: Thomas Sankara Killed
events.body: Burkina Faso's young revolutionary president is shot dead in a coup that brings his comrade Blaise Compaoré to power.

events.title: Black Monday
events.body: Stock markets crash worldwide; the Dow falls 22.6% in a day — still its worst one-day percentage loss ever.

events.title: Enniskillen Bombing
events.body: An IRA bomb kills 11 people at a Remembrance Day service. Gordon Wilson, holding his dying daughter's hand, forgives the bombers — and moves the world.

events.title: Cry Freedom
events.body: Richard Attenborough's film of Donald Woods' friendship with Steve Biko, with Denzel Washington as Biko. Copies are seized in South Africa on the day it opens there.

events.title: King's Cross Fire
events.body: A fire beneath a wooden escalator at King's Cross Underground station kills 31 people and transforms fire safety on the Tube.

events.title: The INF Treaty
events.body: Reagan and Gorbachev sign the first treaty to abolish an entire class of nuclear weapons — scrapping nearly 2,700 intermediate-range missiles.

events.title: Australia's Bicentenary
events.body: Two hundred years after the First Fleet, tall ships fill Sydney Harbour — while tens of thousands march for Aboriginal rights under the banner "White Australia has a Black History".

events.title: Halabja Chemical Attack
events.body: Iraqi forces gas the Kurdish town of Halabja, killing thousands of civilians in the worst chemical attack on a civilian population in history.

events.title: Cuito Cuanavale
events.body: The climactic assault in the largest battle in Africa since El Alamein fails to dislodge Angolan and Cuban forces. The stalemate pushes all sides to the table — and hastens Namibian independence.

events.title: The Crazy Gang Beat Liverpool
events.body: Unfancied Wimbledon stun the league champions 1–0 in the FA Cup final — "the Crazy Gang have beaten the Culture Club".

events.title: Soviets Begin Leaving Afghanistan
events.body: After eight years and some 15,000 Soviet dead, the Red Army starts its withdrawal — a retreat that helps unravel the USSR itself.

events.title: Mandela's 70th Birthday Concert
events.body: Eighty-three artists play Wembley for the imprisoned Nelson Mandela, broadcast to 67 countries — beaming the anti-apartheid cause into 600 million homes.

sources.title: Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute: concert programme

events.title: Who Framed Roger Rabbit Opens
events.body: Live action and animation share the screen as never before — and Disney and Warner Bros characters appear together for the only time.

events.title: Measures of Distance
events.body: Mona Hatoum, a Palestinian exiled in London by the Lebanese civil war, overlays letters from her mother in Beirut on intimate images of her — a video about love and separation across a war.

events.title: Nada, nadie
events.body: Elena Poniatowska gathers the voices of survivors, rescuers and the bereaved of the 1985 Mexico City earthquake — “nothing, no one” — and the government's failure to save them.

events.title: Iran Air 655 Shot Down
events.body: The USS Vincennes mistakes an Iranian airliner for a fighter and destroys it over the Gulf, killing all 290 aboard.

events.title: Piper Alpha
events.body: Explosions destroy the North Sea oil platform, killing 167 men — the world's deadliest offshore disaster, which rewrites safety law for the industry.

events.title: Die Hard Opens
events.body: A New York cop in the wrong skyscraper on Christmas Eve redefines the action film — and launches the "is it a Christmas movie?" debate.

events.title: Iran–Iraq War Ends
events.body: A UN ceasefire silences the guns after eight years and perhaps a million dead — a war that ends almost exactly where it began.

events.title: Seoul Olympics Open
events.body: South Korea hosts the Games as its democracy takes root; 159 nations attend, the Cold War boycotts finally over.

events.title: The Satanic Verses Published
events.body: Salman Rushdie's novel appears in London to strong reviews — and sets off protests, bans, burnings, and within five months a death sentence from Tehran.

events.title: Ben Johnson Stripped of Gold
events.body: Three days after his 9.79-second 100m stuns the world, the Canadian tests positive for stanozolol — sport's most infamous doping scandal.

events.title: The Shuttle Flies Again
events.body: Discovery lifts off — America's return to space 32 months after the Challenger disaster.

events.title: Carbon Dating the Turin Shroud
events.body: Three laboratories independently date the famous relic to the 13th or 14th century — mediaeval, not biblical.

events.title: The Morris Worm
events.body: A Cornell student's experiment escapes his control and cripples a tenth of the early internet — the first great computer-security wake-up call.

events.title: Bush Elected President
events.body: Vice-President George H. W. Bush defeats Michael Dukakis — the first sitting VP to win the White House since 1836.

events.title: Buran's Only Flight
events.body: The Soviet space shuttle flies a flawless two-orbit mission entirely under automatic control — and never flies again as the USSR's money runs out.

events.title: The Bougainville Crisis
events.body: Landowners sabotage the giant Panguna copper mine, starting a decade of war on Bougainville in which thousands die. In 2019, 98 per cent vote for independence.

events.title: Gorbachev at the UN
events.body: The Soviet leader announces unilateral cuts of 500,000 troops and renounces force in Eastern Europe — effectively releasing the satellite states.

events.title: Clapham Junction Rail Crash
events.body: A signalling fault causes a three-train collision in London, killing 35 — and prompting an overhaul of British rail safety.

events.title: Lockerbie
events.body: A bomb destroys Pan Am Flight 103 over the Scottish town of Lockerbie, killing all 259 aboard and 11 on the ground — Britain's deadliest terrorist attack.

events.title: Emperor Hirohito Dies
events.body: Japan's emperor dies at 87 after 62 years on the throne — a reign spanning militarism, war, occupation and the economic miracle. The Heisei era begins.

events.title: Sky TV Launches
events.body: Rupert Murdoch's four-channel satellite service begins broadcasting to Britain — the start of the multichannel era.

events.title: The Rushdie Fatwa
events.body: Ayatollah Khomeini calls for the death of novelist Salman Rushdie over The Satanic Verses, driving him into hiding for a decade.

events.title: Soviets Leave Afghanistan
events.body: General Gromov walks across the Friendship Bridge — officially the last Soviet soldier out of Afghanistan after nine years of war.

events.title: The Web Is Proposed
events.body: At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee circulates "Information Management: A Proposal". His boss scrawls on it: "Vague, but exciting" — and the World Wide Web is conceived.

events.title: Cold Fusion Announced
events.body: Two chemists in Utah claim fusion in a jar at room temperature. The world briefly dreams of free energy — then nobody can replicate it.

events.title: Exxon Valdez
events.body: The tanker runs aground in Alaska's Prince William Sound, spilling roughly 41 million litres of crude along pristine coastline.

events.title: The Louvre Pyramid Opens
events.body: I. M. Pei's glass pyramid — furiously controversial when proposed — opens as the museum's new entrance, and becomes a symbol of Paris.

events.title: Hillsborough
events.body: A crush at an FA Cup semi-final kills 96 Liverpool supporters (a 97th victim is later recognised). Families fight for decades before the truth about police failures is acknowledged.

events.title: Your Body Is a Battleground
events.body: Barbara Kruger's poster for the Washington march defending abortion rights: a woman's face split into positive and negative, cut with the slogan in white-on-red. It becomes one of the defining images of feminist art.

events.title: Game Boy Launches
events.body: Nintendo's grey handheld arrives in Japan bundled with Tetris — and sells over 118 million units worldwide.

events.title: The Stone Roses' Debut
events.body: The Manchester band's first album fuses indie jangle with dance swagger — a cornerstone of the Madchester era and of Britpop to come.

events.title: The Goddess of Democracy
events.body: Art students build a ten-metre figure of foam and papier-mâché in four days and raise it facing Mao's portrait in Tiananmen Square. Five days later the army crushes it with the protest.

events.title: Tiananmen Square
events.body: The Chinese army clears pro-democracy protesters from Beijing with tanks and live fire, killing hundreds or more. The "Tank Man" photograph becomes an icon of defiance.

events.title: Solidarity Sweeps Poland
events.body: In the Eastern bloc's first partly-free elections, Solidarity wins every contested seat it can — the beginning of the end of communist rule in Europe.

events.title: Tank Man
events.body: From a hotel balcony, Jeff Widener and other photographers capture a lone man with shopping bags standing in front of a column of tanks. Who he was, and what became of him, has never been established.

events.title: The Perfect Moment Cancelled
events.body: Washington's Corcoran Gallery cancels Robert Mapplethorpe's retrospective weeks after his death from AIDS, fearing Congress. The decision opens America's “culture wars” over what public money may fund.

events.title: Batman Opens
events.body: Tim Burton's gothic blockbuster, with Jack Nicholson's Joker, ignites "Batmania" and the modern superhero era.

events.title: The End of History?
events.body: Francis Fukuyama's essay argues that liberal democracy may be the end point of humanity's ideological evolution. Published months before the Wall falls, it becomes the most argued-over idea of the decade.

events.title: The Pan-European Picnic
events.body: At a symbolic border opening, hundreds of East Germans dash from Hungary into Austria — the first tear in the Iron Curtain.

events.title: The Marchioness Disaster
events.body: A dredger runs down the pleasure boat Marchioness on the Thames at night; 51 young partygoers drown.

events.title: Voyager 2 at Neptune
events.body: The probe sweeps past Neptune and its moon Triton — the final planetary encounter of the Grand Tour, 12 years after launch.

events.title: The Purple Shall Govern
events.body: Police turn a purple-dyed water cannon on anti-apartheid marchers in Cape Town; a protester seizes the nozzle and sprays it back. Graffiti appears overnight: "The Purple Shall Govern".

events.title: Cape Town Marches for Peace
events.body: Some 30,000 people, led by Desmond Tutu and mayor Gordon Oliver, march on the City Hall — the biggest legal anti-apartheid march in three decades, and De Klerk lets it happen.

events.title: De Klerk Becomes President
events.body: FW de Klerk is sworn in as South Africa's State President. Within six months he will unban the ANC and release Mandela.

events.title: The Berlin Wall Falls
events.body: After a bungled press conference, East Berliners surge to the checkpoints and the guards stand aside. Strangers dance on the Wall all night.

sources.title: The 'astonishing news' of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989
The 1989 Associated Press report from when the Berlin Wall crumbled

events.title: The Velvet Revolution Begins
events.body: Police beat student marchers in Prague; within days hundreds of thousands fill Wenceslas Square. By year's end the playwright Václav Havel is president.

sources.title: Primary sources: November 17, 1989
sources.publisher: Making the History of 1989 (George Mason University)

events.title: The Simpsons Premieres
events.body: The shorts become a full series with a Christmas special — the start of an institution still running more than three decades later.

events.title: US Invades Panama
events.body: American forces topple Manuel Noriega, who takes refuge in the Vatican embassy — where troops famously blast rock music at him until he surrenders.

events.title: Liberia's Civil War
events.body: Charles Taylor's rebels cross into Liberia. Two civil wars follow, ending only in 2003; hundreds of thousands die.

events.title: The Ceaușescus Executed
events.body: Romania's dictator and his wife are tried by a drumhead court and shot on Christmas Day — the only violent end among 1989's revolutions.

events.title: McDonald's Opens in Moscow
events.body: Thirty thousand Muscovites queue in Pushkin Square on opening day — a Big Mac as the taste of a closing Cold War.

events.title: De Klerk Unbans the ANC
events.body: In one parliamentary speech, FW de Klerk legalises the ANC, PAC and SACP and announces Mandela's release. The apartheid endgame begins.

events.title: Mandela Walks Free
events.body: After 27 years, Nelson Mandela walks out of Victor Verster Prison hand in hand with Winnie, fist raised. That evening he speaks to the world from Cape Town's City Hall balcony.

events.title: The Pale Blue Dot
events.body: Voyager 1, 6 billion kilometres out, turns and photographs Earth — a single pale pixel in a sunbeam. "That's here. That's home. That's us," writes Carl Sagan.

events.title: Lithuania Breaks First
events.body: The first Soviet republic declares independence restored — the Baltic crack that widens all year.

events.title: Twin Peaks Premieres
events.body: David Lynch brings arthouse dread to network television. "Who killed Laura Palmer?" grips the world; TV is never quite normal again.

events.title: Hubble Launched
events.body: The space telescope reaches orbit — with a flawed mirror, soon corrected — and goes on to remake humanity's picture of the universe.

events.title: “Wind of Change”
events.body: Klaus Meine of Scorpions writes it after a peace festival in Moscow, whistling as he imagines the Cold War ending. Released on Crazy World, it becomes the soundtrack of the Wall's fall.

events.title: The Things They Carried
events.body: Tim O'Brien's linked stories of an infantry platoon in Vietnam — the weight of the radios, the photographs, the fear — blur memoir and fiction to ask how a war story can ever be true.

events.title: Gazza's Tears
events.body: England lose a World Cup semi-final shoot-out to West Germany in Turin; Paul Gascoigne's tears melt a nation and remake English football's image.

events.title: Iraq Invades Kuwait
events.body: Saddam Hussein's army overruns the emirate in hours. The UN responds with the broadest military coalition since 1945.

events.title: The East Side Gallery
events.body: Artists from around the world paint 1.3 km of the Berlin Wall. Dmitri Vrubel's painting of the Brezhnev–Honecker kiss, “My God, Help Me to Survive This Deadly Love”, becomes the most photographed stretch.

events.title: Germany Reunified
events.body: Less than a year after the Wall fell, the two Germanies become one at midnight before the Reichstag.

events.title: Thatcher Resigns
events.body: Felled by her own party over Europe and the poll tax, the Iron Lady leaves Downing Street in tears after 11 years.

events.title: Haiti's First Free Election
events.body: Radical priest Jean-Bertrand Aristide wins Haiti's first free presidential election by a landslide. He is overthrown by the army nine months later.

events.title: The First Website
events.body: At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee's NeXT computer serves the world's first web page — instructions, naturally, on how to make more web pages.

events.title: Desert Storm Begins
events.body: The air war opens over Baghdad, live on CNN — the first war watched in real time. Kuwait is liberated in six weeks.

events.title: Sierra Leone's Civil War
events.body: The Revolutionary United Front invades from Liberia. The eleven-year war, funded by diamonds, becomes known for mutilations and child soldiers.

events.title: Pinatubo Erupts
events.body: The Philippine volcano's colossal eruption — the century's second largest — kills hundreds and cools the entire planet by half a degree for two years.

events.title: The Red Ribbon
events.body: The Visual AIDS Artists Caucus designs a simple looped red ribbon as a sign of compassion for people with AIDS. Worn on camera at the Tony Awards, it is soon everywhere.

events.title: Apartheid's Pillars Repealed
events.body: South Africa's parliament scraps the Population Registration Act — the law that sorted every citizen by race. The statutory heart of apartheid stops beating.

events.title: Yugoslavia Starts to Break
events.body: Slovenia and Croatia declare independence; within days the Yugoslav army moves. A decade of Balkan wars begins.

events.title: Portrait of Ross in L.A.
events.body: Felix Gonzalez-Torres piles 79 kilos of wrapped sweets in a gallery corner — the ideal body weight of his partner Ross, dying of AIDS. Visitors take a sweet; the pile shrinks, and is replenished.

events.title: The Gulf War Did Not Take Place
events.body: Jean Baudrillard's provocation: that what the West watched on CNN was not a war but an atrocity staged as a media event. Mocked and debated, it still frames talk of war on screens.

events.title: Wild Swans
events.body: Jung Chang tells the lives of her grandmother, a warlord's concubine, her mother, a Communist official, and herself, a Red Guard — a history of 20th-century China banned in the country it describes.

events.title: Terminator 2 Opens
events.body: Liquid metal walks: Cameron's sequel makes computer-generated imagery the new engine of spectacle.

events.title: The Web Goes Public
events.body: Berners-Lee posts the World Wide Web's code and summary to an internet newsgroup — free, for everyone, forever.

events.title: The August Coup
events.body: Hardliners detain Gorbachev and send tanks into Moscow; Yeltsin climbs onto one outside the White House. The coup collapses in three days — and takes the USSR's authority with it.

events.title: Iron Felix Toppled
events.body: As the coup collapses, crowds in Moscow cheer as a crane lifts the statue of Felix Dzerzhinsky, founder of the secret police, from its plinth outside the KGB headquarters.

events.title: Linux Announced
events.body: A Finnish student posts about his hobby operating system — "won't be big and professional". It ends up running most of the internet.

events.title: Ötzi Emerges from the Ice
events.body: Hikers in the Alps find a body melting out of a glacier — a 5,300-year-old man with his axe, clothes and unfinished business intact.

events.title: Nevermind Released
events.body: Nirvana's second album drags the underground into the mainstream; within months it knocks Michael Jackson off No 1.

events.title: Freddie Mercury Dies
events.body: Queen's frontman dies of AIDS a day after confirming his illness — the disease's most famous casualty, and a turning point in public attitudes.

events.title: The Soviet Union Dissolves
events.body: Gorbachev resigns and the red flag comes down over the Kremlin. Seventy-four years of the USSR end not with war but a signature.

events.title: Algeria's Dark Decade
events.body: With an Islamist party about to win elections, Algeria's army cancels the vote. The civil war that follows kills somewhere between 100,000 and 200,000 people, by most estimates.

events.title: The Maastricht Treaty
events.body: Twelve nations sign the treaty that creates the European Union and commits to a single currency.

events.title: Whites Vote to End Apartheid
events.body: In South Africa's last whites-only referendum, 68.7% vote to continue the reform process — De Klerk's gamble pays off, and there is no turning back.

events.title: The Siege of Sarajevo Begins
events.body: Bosnian Serb forces encircle the city; the longest siege in modern history will last 1,425 days.

sources.title: April 5, 1992: the siege of Sarajevo begins

events.title: The LA Riots
events.body: Acquittals in the Rodney King beating ignite six days of violence that kill 63 — America's racial fault line laid bare on live television.

events.title: The Cellist of Sarajevo
events.body: After a shell kills people queuing for bread, cellist Vedran Smailović plays Albinoni's Adagio in the ruins in his concert tails — and keeps playing at funerals and bomb sites for twenty-two days.

events.title: The Rio Earth Summit
events.body: The largest gathering of world leaders yet held signs conventions on climate and biodiversity — the framework for every climate fight since.

events.title: The Mabo Decision
events.body: Australia's High Court rules for Eddie Mabo and the Meriam people, overturning the idea that the land was terra nullius — 'nobody's land' — when the British arrived.

events.title: The Boipatong Massacre
events.body: Forty-five residents of a Vaal township are massacred; the ANC suspends talks with the government. The transition nearly dies here.

events.title: Barcelona Opens the Games
events.body: An archer lights the cauldron with a flaming arrow; the Dream Team plays; post-Franco Spain announces itself to the world.

events.title: The Premier League Kicks Off
events.body: English football's breakaway top flight plays its first matches — satellite money is about to remake the world's game.

events.title: Sarajevo's Library Burns
events.body: Bosnian Serb shells set the National and University Library alight. Citizens form chains to carry books out under fire; well over a million volumes are lost. An echo of Louvain, 78 years before.

events.title: Black Wednesday
events.body: Speculators led by George Soros force sterling out of Europe's exchange-rate mechanism; Britain burns billions defending the indefensible.

events.title: Sinéad Tears the Photograph
events.body: Live on Saturday Night Live, Sinéad O'Connor sings Bob Marley's “War”, holds up a photograph of Pope John Paul II and tears it apart — a protest against abuse in the Church that wrecks her career and is later seen as prophetic.

events.title: Clinton Elected
events.body: The Arkansas governor beats George Bush as the economy sours — "It's the economy, stupid."

events.title: The Church of England Votes for Women Priests
events.body: After decades of argument, the General Synod says yes by two votes — the first ordinations follow within sixteen months.

events.title: Windsor Castle Burns
events.body: Fire guts more than a hundred rooms of the Queen's favourite home, capping what she calls her annus horribilis.

events.title: The First Text Message
events.body: An engineer sends "Merry Christmas" from a computer to a phone on Vodafone's network — SMS is born, brevity follows.

events.title: The Velvet Divorce
events.body: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia at midnight — the gentlest break-up of the age.

events.title: The World Trade Center Bombing
events.body: A truck bomb in the basement garage kills six and injures a thousand — the towers survive, and the warning goes unheeded.

events.title: The Pentium Arrives
events.body: Intel's new chip brings workstation power to the desktop — and "Intel Inside" to the world's advertising breaks.

events.title: The Struggling Girl
events.body: Kevin Carter's photograph of a starving child in Sudan, a vulture waiting behind her, is published in The New York Times. It wins the Pulitzer; months later Carter, haunted by what he had seen, takes his own life.

events.title: Chris Hani Assassinated
events.body: A white extremist guns down the SACP leader outside his home; a white neighbour's quick action catches the killer. Mandela's televised appeal for calm steadies a nation on the brink.

events.title: Jurassic Park Opens
events.body: Spielberg's dinosaurs fuse animatronics and CGI so convincingly that cinema's relationship with the impossible changes overnight.

events.title: Women of Allah
events.body: After returning to Iran in 1990 for the first time since the revolution, Shirin Neshat begins photographs of veiled women with Persian poetry inked across their hands and faces — and rifles in their arms.

events.title: Zlata's Diary
events.body: An eleven-year-old girl's diary of the siege of Sarajevo, from birthday parties to shelling and cellars, is published in the besieged city and then around the world.

events.title: Buckingham Palace Opens Its Doors
events.body: Tourists are admitted to the state rooms for the first time — £8 a head, to help pay for the Windsor fire.

events.title: The X-Files Premieres
events.body: Two FBI agents, one poster: I Want to Believe. Conspiracy culture gets its defining show.

events.title: The Oslo Handshake
events.body: Rabin and Arafat shake hands on the White House lawn over an agreement negotiated in secret in Norway — the closest the conflict has come to peace.

events.title: Black Hawk Down
events.body: A raid in Mogadishu collapses into an overnight battle; 18 American soldiers and hundreds of Somalis die, and US appetite for intervention dies with them.

events.title: Mandela and De Klerk Share the Nobel
events.body: The prize honours the two men dismantling apartheid together — allies in purpose, adversaries in everything else.

events.title: House
events.body: Rachel Whiteread casts the inside of a condemned Victorian terrace house in east London in concrete. Loved, loathed, awarded the Turner Prize — and demolished by the council within three months.

events.title: The Stari Most Falls
events.body: Croatian forces shell Mostar's 16th-century Ottoman bridge into the Neretva. Its destruction becomes a symbol of a war on culture and memory; it is rebuilt stone by stone and reopens in 2004.

events.title: “Streets of Philadelphia”
events.body: Bruce Springsteen's quiet song for the film Philadelphia, Hollywood's first major film about AIDS. It wins the Oscar and four Grammys.

events.title: The First Women Priests
events.body: Thirty-two women are ordained in Bristol Cathedral — the Church of England's four-century male monopoly ends.

events.title: Kurt Cobain Dies
events.body: Nirvana's songwriter takes his own life at 27 in Seattle — grunge's reluctant figurehead becomes its casualty.

events.title: The Rwandan Genocide Begins
events.body: The president's plane is shot down over Kigali; within hours the killing starts. In a hundred days, some 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu are murdered as the world looks away.

sources.title: Historical background: the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda

events.title: South Africa Votes
events.body: Queues snake for kilometres as all South Africans vote together for the first time. Four days of voting, no civil war — the miracle, delivered.

sources.title: First democratic elections in South Africa (1994 report)

events.title: Senna Dies at Imola
events.body: Ayrton Senna's Williams leaves the track at Tamburello at 300 km/h, a day after Roland Ratzenberger's death. Formula 1 rebuilds itself around safety; Brazil mourns for days.

events.title: The Channel Tunnel Opens
events.body: The Queen and President Mitterrand cut the ribbon under the sea — Britain joined to the continent for the first time since the Ice Age.

events.title: President Mandela
events.body: Nelson Mandela is inaugurated at the Union Buildings before the largest gathering of world leaders since Kennedy's funeral — jets of the air force he now commands trailing the new flag's colours.

events.title: “Zombie”
events.body: Dolores O'Riordan writes it in grief and fury after an IRA bomb kills two children in Warrington. The Cranberries release it the same year the IRA declares its ceasefire.

events.title: The Rwanda Project
events.body: Alfredo Jaar travels to Rwanda in the genocide's aftermath and takes thousands of photographs — then, over six years, finds ways not to show them: boxed, described, withheld, asking why the world looked away.

events.title: Long Walk to Freedom
events.body: Nelson Mandela's autobiography, begun in secret on Robben Island and smuggled out in pieces, is published in the first year of his presidency.

events.title: Comet Strikes Jupiter
events.body: Shoemaker-Levy 9's fragments slam into Jupiter with scars larger than Earth — the first planetary impact ever watched live, and a memo about planetary defence.

events.title: The IRA Ceasefire
events.body: After 25 years of armed campaign, the IRA announces a complete cessation of operations — the long road to peace opens.

events.title: The Estonia Sinks
events.body: The ferry's bow door fails in a Baltic storm; 852 die — Europe's worst peacetime maritime disaster since the war.

events.title: Pulp Fiction Opens
events.body: Tarantino's looping, talkative crime picture wins the Palme d'Or and makes independent film the decade's main event.

events.title: The PlayStation Launches
events.body: Sony enters gaming in Japan after Nintendo jilts its CD partnership — a grudge that reshapes an industry.

events.title: The Kobe Earthquake
events.body: A magnitude-6.9 quake kills over 6,400 in Japan's sixth-largest city and rewrites earthquake engineering worldwide.

events.title: Sarin on the Tokyo Subway
events.body: The Aum Shinrikyo cult releases nerve gas on rush-hour trains, killing 14 and injuring thousands — chemical terror arrives in a modern metropolis.

events.title: Oklahoma City
events.body: A truck bomb destroys the Murrah Federal Building, killing 168 — the deadliest act of home-grown terrorism in American history.

events.title: The Springboks' World Cup
events.body: Mandela, wearing the No 6 Springbok jersey, hands Francois Pienaar the trophy at Ellis Park after extra time against the All Blacks — one team, one country.

events.title: Wrapped Reichstag
events.body: After 24 years of lobbying, Christo and Jeanne-Claude wrap the Reichstag in silver fabric. Five million people come to see the building of a divided past wrapped before its rebirth as the parliament of a united Germany.

events.title: Srebrenica
events.body: Bosnian Serb forces murder more than 8,000 men and boys in a UN "safe area" — Europe's worst atrocity since the Second World War.

events.title: Amazon Opens for Business
events.body: A Seattle start-up sells its first book online. The everything store starts with paper.

events.title: Windows 95 Launches
events.body: Midnight queues for an operating system: Start menu, taskbar, and the Rolling Stones' Start Me Up. The PC becomes a household appliance.

events.title: The O.J. Verdict
events.body: A hundred million people stop to watch the acquittal — the trial of the century ends and the arguments never do.

events.title: The First Exoplanet
events.body: Swiss astronomers announce 51 Pegasi b, a planet orbiting another sun — the first of thousands, and the end of our solar system's monopoly.

events.title: Rabin Assassinated
events.body: An Israeli extremist shoots the prime minister at a Tel Aviv peace rally. In his pocket, a blood-stained song sheet for the Song of Peace.

events.title: Ken Saro-Wiwa Hanged
events.body: Nigeria's military government hangs the Ogoni writer and environmental campaigner and eight others after a trial widely condemned as unjust. Nigeria is suspended from the Commonwealth.

events.title: The Dayton Accords
events.body: Three weeks on an Ohio airbase end the Bosnian war — an imperfect peace that has held ever since.

events.title: Toy Story Opens
events.body: The first entirely computer-animated feature film — Pixar's gamble turns toys into the future of animation.

events.title: The Docklands Bomb
events.body: The IRA ends its 17-month ceasefire with a massive bomb at Canary Wharf, killing two — and jolting the peace process back to life.

events.title: Trainspotting Opens
events.body: Danny Boyle's heroin-black comedy bottles 90s Britain — Choose Life enters the vernacular.

events.title: Pokémon Launches
events.body: Red and Green go on sale for the Game Boy in Japan — catching them all becomes the world's most valuable media franchise.

events.title: Dunblane
events.body: A gunman murders sixteen five- and six-year-olds and their teacher in a Scottish primary school. Within two years Britain bans handguns outright.

events.title: The TRC Begins
events.body: Archbishop Tutu opens the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's first hearings in East London — victims speak, perpetrators confess, a nation listens to itself.

events.title: Dolly Is Born
events.body: A lamb cloned from an adult udder cell is born in Scotland — proof that a body cell's clock can be wound back, and a storm when revealed.

events.title: Wannabe Released
events.body: The Spice Girls' debut single tops charts in 37 countries; Girl Power becomes the phrase of the decade.

events.title: Life on Mars?
events.body: NASA announces possible fossil microbes in Martian meteorite ALH84001. The claim fades; the astrobiology boom it starts does not.

events.title: Tupac Shakur Dies
events.body: Hip-hop's most magnetic star dies six days after a Las Vegas drive-by, at 25 — the East–West feud's most grievous loss.

events.title: The Taliban Take Kabul
events.body: The movement sweeps into the Afghan capital and imposes its rule — the war that never ended enters a darker phase.

events.title: A Constitution Signed at Sharpeville
events.body: Mandela signs South Africa's final Constitution at the site of the 1960 massacre — among the most admired constitutions in the world.

events.title: Dolly Revealed
events.body: Roslin announces the clone to the world; Dolly becomes the most famous sheep in history and bioethics gets its defining argument.

events.title: The Notorious B.I.G. Dies
events.body: Biggie Smalls is killed in a Los Angeles drive-by at 24, six months after Tupac — the coastal feud consumes its second giant.

events.title: Blair's Landslide
events.body: New Labour ends 18 years of Conservative rule with a 179-seat majority. "A new dawn has broken, has it not?"

events.title: Deep Blue Beats Kasparov
events.body: IBM's machine defeats the world chess champion over a match — the first time silicon beats humanity's best at its most cerebral game.

events.title: OK Computer Released
events.body: Radiohead's pre-millennium unease — praised, dissected, and voted the best album of its generation ever since.

events.title: Harry Potter Published
events.body: Bloomsbury prints 500 copies of a rejected manuscript about a boy wizard. A generation learns to read by torchlight.

events.title: Hong Kong Handed Back
events.body: At midnight the Union Jack comes down and China resumes sovereignty — the effective end of the British Empire, in the rain.

events.title: Ubu and the Truth Commission
events.body: William Kentridge and the Handspring Puppet Company stage Jarry's monstrous King Ubu inside the testimony of the Truth Commission, with animation and puppets standing in for witnesses whose words are real.

events.title: Underground
events.body: Haruki Murakami interviews survivors of the sarin attack, and later members of Aum Shinrikyo, to understand what the Tokyo subway attack revealed about Japan.

events.title: Voices from Chernobyl
events.body: Svetlana Alexievich spends years recording the firemen's widows, evacuees and liquidators of Chernobyl, weaving their testimony into an oral history. In 2015 she wins the Nobel Prize.

events.title: The Asian Crisis Begins
events.body: Thailand floats the baht and currencies topple across East Asia — globalisation's first great financial contagion.

events.title: Pathfinder Lands on Mars
events.body: A lander wrapped in airbags bounces onto Mars and releases Sojourner, the first rover on another planet; the mission's website breaks every traffic record.

events.title: Versace Murdered
events.body: Gianni Versace is shot dead on his Miami Beach steps by a spree killer — fashion loses its great showman at 50.

events.title: Diana Dies in Paris
events.body: The Princess of Wales is killed in a car crash pursued by paparazzi. Britain drowns in flowers; the monarchy bends before the grief.

events.title: Mother Teresa Dies
events.body: The nun of the Calcutta gutters dies at 87, five days after Diana — two global icons of compassion gone in a week.

events.title: The Guggenheim Bilbao
events.body: Frank Gehry's titanium swirls open in a rusting port city — and "the Bilbao effect" enters every mayor's vocabulary.

events.title: The Kyoto Protocol
events.body: Nations adopt the first binding treaty to cut greenhouse gases — the start of the long, unfinished climate bargain.

events.title: Titanic Opens
events.body: Cameron's shipwreck epic, the most expensive film ever made, becomes the highest-grossing — and sails on for fifteen Oscars nominations.

events.title: Viagra Approved
events.body: The failed angina drug with the memorable side effect gets its licence — and becomes the fastest-selling medicine in history.

events.title: The Good Friday Agreement
events.body: After 30 years and 3,500 dead, Northern Ireland's parties sign a peace deal on Good Friday. Referendums north and south say yes.

events.title: Truth Games
events.body: Sue Williamson builds interactive panels from Truth Commission hearings: slide the slats and the faces of victims, perpetrators and their words move together and apart.

events.title: We Wish to Inform You That Tomorrow We Will Be Killed with Our Families
events.body: Philip Gourevitch's account of the Rwandan genocide and its aftermath, taking its title from a letter written by Tutsi pastors to their church leader — and asking how the world allowed it.

events.title: Country of My Skull
events.body: Poet Antjie Krog, who reported on the Truth Commission for SABC radio, writes its story in prose, poetry and testimony — an Afrikaner's reckoning with what her people did.

events.title: France Win Their World Cup
events.body: Zidane heads two in the final as the hosts beat Brazil 3–0 — a multiracial team crowned, for a moment, as the face of the nation.

events.title: Africa's World War Begins
events.body: The Second Congo War draws in nine nations; by its end it is the deadliest conflict since 1945.

events.title: The Embassy Bombings
events.body: Al-Qaeda truck bombs destroy the US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam, killing 224 — the network announces itself to the world.

events.title: Omagh
events.body: A Real IRA car bomb kills 29 people four months after the peace deal — the Troubles' deadliest single attack, and, in its horror, a seal on the peace.

events.title: The iMac Launches
events.body: Jobs, back at a dying Apple, ships a translucent blue computer with no floppy drive. Design sells; Apple's resurrection begins.

events.title: Google Founded
events.body: Two Stanford students incorporate their search engine in a Menlo Park garage. Within years, its name is a verb.

events.title: The TRC Reports
events.body: Tutu hands Mandela five volumes of the nation's confessed sins — unflinching about all sides, and contested by all sides.

events.title: Hurricane Mitch
events.body: The storm stalls over Central America and kills more than 11,000 — the Atlantic's deadliest hurricane in two centuries.

events.title: The ISS Begins
events.body: Russia launches Zarya, the first module of the International Space Station — old enemies start building a shared home in orbit.

events.title: Clinton Impeached
events.body: The House impeaches the president over the Lewinsky affair; the Senate acquits. The scandal devours a year of American public life.

events.title: The Euro Is Born
events.body: Eleven currencies lock together as the euro launches on financial markets — notes and coins follow in 2002.

events.title: The Sopranos Premieres
events.body: A mobster walks into therapy. Television's third golden age starts in a New Jersey strip mall.

events.title: Chávez Takes Office
events.body: Hugo Chávez, a former paratrooper who once led a failed coup, becomes president of Venezuela promising a 'Bolivarian revolution'.

events.title: NATO Bombs Yugoslavia
events.body: The alliance goes to war over Kosovo without UN sanction — 78 days of bombing until Belgrade yields.

events.title: The Matrix Opens
events.body: Bullet time, black coats and a question about reality — the film the internet age chose as its myth.

events.title: Columbine
events.body: Two students murder thirteen at their Colorado high school — the massacre that makes "school shooting" a permanent American category.

events.title: United's Impossible Treble
events.body: Two stoppage-time goals in Barcelona beat Bayern and complete Manchester United's League, Cup and European treble. "Football, bloody hell."

events.title: Napster Launches
events.body: A teenager's file-sharing program puts every song everywhere, free. The music industry's old world has two years to live.

events.title: Mandela Hands Over
events.body: Thabo Mbeki is inaugurated as Nelson Mandela, 80, retires after a single term — the rarest act in politics, the voluntary exit.

events.title: The Mild Mild West
events.body: On a wall in Stokes Croft, Bristol, a then-unknown graffiti artist paints a teddy bear lobbing a Molotov cocktail at three riot police — a comment on clashes between police and the city's free-party scene. It makes Banksy's name.

events.title: The Last Eclipse of the Millennium
events.body: Totality crosses Cornwall and Europe — the most-watched solar eclipse in history.

events.title: The İzmit Earthquake
events.body: A magnitude-7.6 quake on the North Anatolian fault kills more than 17,000 in Turkey's industrial heartland.

events.title: Six Billion People
events.body: The UN names a baby born in Sarajevo the symbolic six-billionth human — twelve years after the fifth billion.

events.title: The Y2K Watch
events.body: The world holds its breath over a two-digit date bug as midnight rolls west. Planes do not fall; the fixers, having fixed it, get no parade.

events.title: The Panama Canal Handed Over
events.body: At noon on the century's last day, the United States transfers the canal to Panama — 85 years after the first ship steamed through.

events.title: Yeltsin Resigns
events.body: Russia's first elected president quits unexpectedly on New Year's Eve, asking forgiveness — and hands power to his prime minister, Vladimir Putin.
